source: Bezakova, Galanis, Goldberg, Guo, Stefankovic, SICOMP 2019 (arXiv:1510.09193); Moitra JACM 2019; Galanis-Guo-Wang
statement: Approximate #SAT of (k,Delta)-CNF: FPTAS for Delta <= c*2^(k/2)/k (Moitra); NP-hard (NP=RP) for Delta >= c*2^(k/2). Threshold exponent k/2.

conclusion: For F0 unsatisfiable with j=min{i:a_i>0} and F_t = F0 AND (t disjoint satisfiable 3-clauses on fresh vars), the shifted polynomial P(lambda)=Z_F(lambda)+c (c>0) has j zeros within 2(c/(A0 7^t))^(1/j)=2^-Omega(t) of [0,1] (Rouche on |lambda|=R_t). So no class containing an UNSAT formula and closed under fresh-clause padding has a uniform-width zero-free neighbourhood of [0,1] for P.
justification: Z multiplicative over variable-disjoint conjunction; Rouche comparison c+A lambda^j h vs c+A lambda^j; exact finite check on F0=all 8 clauses on 3 vars matches 1/(16 7^t)

approach: O2: decide SAT beyond the always-satisfiable region via an instance-dependent zero-free (Lee-Yang/Barvinok) criterion on Z_F

why: Zero-free interpolation computes #SAT only on the counting-tractable region (degree <~ 2^(k/2)/k), which is exponentially below f(k)~2^k/k (SAT trivial, all-YES) and a factor ~k below the counting-hardness threshold 2^(k/2). It cannot reach the NP-hard decision regime. On padded classes the forced zero cannot be shifted away (Z2, PROVEN). Earlier ETH argument (Z3) superseded by this degree-threshold placement.

statement: Approximate counting and sampling of CSP solutions are tractable in the regime 4e*p*(D+1)^2 <= 1 (p=max violation prob, D=max dependency degree); tight up to constants under NP!=RP. The exp-small distance of Z2 appears ONLY for Z+c with fixed c (d: 6.25e-2,1.28e-3,2.60e-5 for t=0,2,4); dividing by 7^t restores constant distance ~0.064. => normalization artifact.

evidence: Normalization test cm-673ff95932cb4a11: zeros of Z itself under padding lie only at 0 (=#SAT) and -7; the near-[0,1] zero is produced solely by adding a FIXED constant c to a polynomial whose coefficients grow like 7^t, and vanishes under division by 7^t or 2^n. The Rouche computation is correct; its reading as an intrinsic/universal obstruction is withdrawn.

conclusion: Proposition O1-E: the smooth-restriction/polar-intersection method (Sheshadri Thm 3.1 / OpenAI) applied to perm_n via affine restrictions cannot prove any lower bound exceeding (n^2-1)(n-1)/(4e) < n^3/(4e) (resp. n^3/(8e) for Pfaffians), because an affine restriction F' of perm_n has degree <= n and, by smoothness (else the zero locus is a cone), <= n^2 variables, and dc(F') <= dc(perm_n).
justification: dc(F')<=dc(perm_n) by pullback of a determinantal rep under the affine map; degree non-increasing under affine substitution; N'<=n^2 forced by smoothness. Independently verified VALID by adversarial reviewer (strong model) with the cone/singularity sharpening of N'<=n^2.

conclusion: Lemma O1-C: pc(F) <= 2 dc(F) via B=[[0,A],[-A^T,0]] (alternating order 2m, Pf B = (-1)^{m(m-1)/2} det A, sign fixed to + by a transposition); and det(M)=Pf(M)^2 gives dc(F^2) <= pc(F). A LINEAR reverse dc(F) <= C*pc(F) is NOT known (only polynomial via VP_ws-completeness); the det->Pf (easy) vs Pf->det (needs a square root, not linear) asymmetry is genuine.
justification: Block-embedding identity with exact sign; VP_ws polynomial equivalence. Verified VALID by adversarial reviewer, who supplied the exact raw sign (-1)^{m(m-1)/2} and the transposition fix.

source: standard (Jacobian criterion; Pfaffian adjugate); owner-sharpened 2026-11-17; verified by adversarial review
statement: Singular criterion for affine Pfaffian reps F(x)=Pf(A_0+sum x_i A_i): x in Sing(V(F)) iff F(x)=0 AND DF_x=0, iff corank A(x)>=4 OR (corank A(x)=2 and u^T A_i v=0 for all i), where u,v span ker A(x). At corank 2, D(Pf)_M(H)=c_M u^T H v with c_M=Pf(A')!=0 (adjugate ~ uv^T-vu^T). Intrinsic locus (corank>=4) codim 6; tangency condition codim 1.

summary: Counterexample A(x,y)=[[0,1,x,0],[-1,0,0,-y],[-x,0,0,0],[0,y,0,0]]: Pf(A)=xy exactly; A(0,0) corank 2 (kernel e3,e4); grad Pf dual to (3,4)-entry; (A_1)_{34}=(A_2)_{34}=0 so im(L) in tangent hyperplane. Origin is tangency-induced (corank 2), NOT intrinsic (corank 4).

conclusion: Lemma T8-B: at a tangency-induced singular point p of F=Pf(A(x)) (A(p) corank 2, kernel u,v, u^T A_i v=0 for all i), rank Hess_F(p) <= 4m-4.
justification: Pfaffian Schur-complement Pf([[X,Y],[-Y^T,Z]])=Pf(Z)Pf(X + Y Z^-1 Y^T) (sign + verified exactly); tangency makes (H11)_12=u^T H v identically 0, so F is quadratic-leading through the 2x(2m-2) block H12; Hessian factors through H12, dim 4m-4. Elementary corollary of the classical Schur identity, NOT a deep theorem. Verified: PI derivation + gpt-oss-120b (independent, gave sign minus) + exact sympy (rank=8=4m-4 tight, 40 random instances by the reviewer never exceed 4m-4) + adversarial review VALID WITH FIXES (sign +, downgrade 'original').

conclusion: Corank-stratified Hessian bounds for affine Pfaffian reps F=Pf(A(x)) at a singular point p: corank 2 => rank Hess_F(p) <= 4m-4 (T8-B); corank 4 => rank <= 6; corank >=6 => rank = 0. Corollary: rank Hess_F(p) > 6 ==> corank A(p)=2.
justification: corank-4: split off invertible skew block, residual 4x4 kernel-Pfaffian quadratic in its 6 entries; corank>=6: kernel-Pfaffian expansion starts at order>=3. Verified exactly (sympy, m=4): corank-4 rank=6 (tight), corank-6 rank=0; corank-2 rank=8=4m-4 (m=3). Independent review of the corank-2 case VALID (T8-B); corank-4/6 derivations under review.

conclusion: Corank-4 bound PROVEN (normal form, not finite search): at a singular point p of F=Pf(A(x)) with corank A(p)=4, rank Hess_F(p) <= 6. Corank>=6 bound PROVEN: rank Hess_F(p)=0.
justification: Pfaffian Schur complement F=Pf(A'+H22)Pf(H11 + H12(A'+H22)^-1 H12^T). Corank 4: DPf=0 (no linear term); Pf of 4x4 is the homogeneous quadratic af-be+cd, so the degree-2 part of F is Pf(A')Pf(H11), factoring through the 6 entries of the 4x4 kernel block H11 => rank<=6. Corank>=6: Pf of 2r x 2r (r>=3) is homogeneous of degree r>=3, so F starts at order>=3 => Hessian=0. Elementary via the local Pfaffian normal form. Numerically consistent (rank 6 tight, 0) but the PROOF is the normal form, not the finite check.

conclusion: Corollary (THEOREM, from the proven corank-stratified bounds): for an affine Pfaffian representation F=Pf(A(x)), rank Hess_F(p) > 6 implies corank A(p) = 2.
justification: A singular point with Hessian rank >6 cannot be corank 4 (<=6) or >=6 (=0), so it is corank 2. Now proven (not just tested), so the unconditional bound pc=2m >= (rank+4)/2 for any such point is rigorous.

statement: Honest status: X_n (two zero rows, rank Hess=2n>6) forces corank 2 and gives m >= (n+2)/2 UNCONDITIONALLY, but this is WEAKER than the degree bound m>=n (perm_n degree n = Pf-degree m). The block-diagonal construction (M_n>=floor(n^2/2)+2) gives the stronger quadratic m>=(floor(n^2/2)+6)/4, which exceeds the degree bound but stays below Sheshadri's cubic. D-016e: Cycle RC-0bd8fd6a (cm in research-atlas.jsonl): C mod 2 = covering parity (number of choices, per clause, of a singleton or the full triple whose union is all n variables, mod 2); checked 777/777. Proof (director, 3 lines): over GF(2) the exactly-one indicator of a clause abc is a+b+c+abc (from a+b+c-2(ab+ac+bc)+3abc); so C = sum_x prod_clauses(...) mod 2; expanding chooses one term per clause, giving the monomial x^U with U the union; sum_x x^U = 2^(n-|U|), odd iff U = all variables. Not novel (standard GF(2) polynomial counting); valid as a reformulation. The run's second part (does the inclusion-exclusion table cost track the frontier-DP state count) is not assessed here. 2026-11-18

CAVEAT: not controlled for m - the number of terms is 2^m and cycle rank grows with m, so the correlation may be an m effect; needs partial correlation at fixed m (or fixed n, m) before any reading. D-014f: Single-difference cap: if every nonzero entry A[u,v] of a Gal matrix has |v \ u| = 1, then rank(A) <= sum_j rank(A|R_j) <= k * max_j rank(A|R_j), so the Gal ratio is at most k = C(n,3). Proof (director): such an entry lies in exactly one clause rectangle R_j = {u: j not in u} x {v: j in v} (j = the unique element of v \ u), so the supports of the restrictions A|R_j are pairwise disjoint and A = sum_j A|R_j; rank is subadditive over a sum. Hence any improvement over k must use entries with |v \ u| >= 2 (where the rectangles overlap and subadditivity fails). Empirically consistent: cycle RC-8fd9326f, n=5 and n=6 over GF(2)/GF(3), 20 trials each, 0 cap violations, sum identity holds. 2026-11-18

The point x = 1/3 is separated in 34.8% of instances (SAT 32.0% of 556; UNSAT 100% of only 24), ALWAYS via non-integer multipliers (integer-multiplier separations: 0), and depth-1 CG never refutes an UNSAT instance (0%). The "integer multipliers never separate" part is TRIVIAL, proved by the director: an integer combination of the equalities has integer coefficients a_i = sum of u_j over clauses containing i and right side b = sum_j u_j; at x = 1/3 its left side is (1/3) sum_i a_i = sum_j u_j = b exactly, so rounding changes nothing and no cut separates 1/3. Hence all separation needs fractional multipliers (the run's half-integer ones); the UNSAT sample is small (24) and the instances are the small enumerated ones, so the "mod-2 effect" reading is NOT established here. Not independently recomputed. 2026-11-18

statement: D-014h: On the domain rows = maxterms u (maximal SAT selections), columns = minterms v (minimal UNSAT selections) of ANY monotone f, u strictly contained in v forces |v \ u| = 1: for c in v \ u, u + c is UNSAT (u maximal SAT) and contained in v; if |v \ u| >= 2 it is a proper subset of the minimal UNSAT v, hence SAT - contradiction. So every containment-incidence family A[u,v] != 0 only for u < v (cycle RC-fbc21332's proposal, any signs) is a single-difference family and is capped at ratio <= N by D-014f. Multi-difference support on this domain needs entries with u NOT contained in v. 2026-11-18

statement: D-020: The D-013 obstruction (P4 minor => not a matroid port) also occurs for 2-SAT, a polynomial-time (NL-complete) problem: 2-SAT on 3 variables with (x0|~x1),(x0|x1),(~x1|x2) present and a=(~x0|~x1), b=(~x0|x1), c=(~x0|~x2), d=(~x0|x2) free has UNSAT = ab|bc|cd (exhaustive minor search lab/transfer/p4_control.py; hand-checked by an independent referee). Calibrations: no P4 in 1in3 n=5 (GF(3) port) or XOR-SAT n=4 (GF(2) port). So "not a matroid port" holds for 2-SAT for all n >= 3 and cannot imply any super-linear circuit lower bound; D-013 measures field-linearity (it separates 1in3 only from XOR-SAT, a GF(2) port by construction), not hardness. D-013 stays a theorem about ideal secret sharing / ideal monotone span programs and is RETIRED as a proof route. Also proved (T45): the owner's subfunction bound S >= log2 D_k - 1 is true but capped at N-1 for every f; direct-sum amplification of fixed obstructions is capped at O(N); exact transfer lemma (superpolynomial infinitely often suffices; P-uniform lower bound is equivalent to P != NP). 2026-11-18

statement: D-022: Depth-1 branching never helps GF(3)-linear refutation of positive 1-in-3: if S is GF(3)-consistent with y in Sol_3(S), then y + lambda*j is in Sol_3(S) for every lambda (j = all-ones is in the kernel, T44), and its i-th coordinate y_i + lambda takes every value of GF(3); so S plus {x_i = b} is consistent for both b in {0,1}. D-014m: STAR CAP (generalizes D-014f): if every clause block A|R_j is a star (its support lies in one row or one column, its "centre" c_j), then rank(A) <= k = C(n,3), over every field. Proof: a nonzero entry (u,v) lies in some R_j, hence in the support of the star A|R_j, so u = c_j or v = c_j; the <= k centres are lines covering every nonzero entry, so the term rank, and hence the rank, is <= k (Konig). Proof given by the referee (claude-haiku) in cycle RC-d0db1c00, checked by the director. Realized star constructions (cycle RC-d0db1c00, not independently recomputed): 1in3 n=5 GF(3) ratio 10 = the TRUE mSP_GF3 = 10 (D-012) - the first Gal construction in PNP-001 that reaches the exact value (previous best 5/2); 1in3 n=6 GF(3) ratio 19 (below D-013's 21, so no improvement); XOR n=5 GF(2) ratio 19 (known <= 20; control non-degenerate: 1,025,439 UNSAT inputs). Consequence: star blocks can never pass k; beating k needs blocks of rank 1 whose support is NOT a star (two disjoint nonzeros) - consistent with D-014g's open case. 2026-11-18

RETRACTED (replaces S-74941caa26). 'Blind rows are exactly those with no GF(3) solution of A x = 1 in {0,1}^n' is a restatement of sat=0, not an explanation. For x in {0,1}^n, a clause sum x_a+x_b+x_c is in {0,1,2,3} and is congruent to 1 mod 3 only when it equals 1. The real question is how the GF(3) affine solution set (dimension null3, coset structure) meets the 0/1 cube, which is the NP-hard core of the problem and is not reduced by this observation.

source: Schaefer, STOC 1978 (owner deep research 2026-11-19; not re-read by the director)
statement: Schaefer dichotomy (1978): a Boolean CSP is in P if every relation is 0-valid, 1-valid, Horn, dual-Horn, bijunctive (2-SAT) or affine over GF(2); otherwise NP-complete. Positive 1-in-3-SAT is none of these, hence NP-complete; a poly-time algorithm for it would prove P = NP.

source: Cai, Lu, Xia, 'Holographic algorithms with matchgates capture precisely tractable planar #CSP' (owner deep research 2026-11-19; not re-read by the director)
statement: Holographic algorithms (Valiant; Cai-Lu-Xia): holographic transformations to matchgates make some planar counting CSPs polynomial that are #P-hard on general graphs; tractability is tied to planarity/structural conditions.

source: Yannakakis, JCSS 1991; Fiorini et al. STOC 2012 (owner deep research 2026-11-19; not re-read by the director)
statement: Yannakakis: symmetric extended LP formulations of TSP / matching polytopes need exponential size (Swart's P=NP LP refuted); Fiorini et al. 2012 removed the symmetry assumption for TSP.

statement: Refuted P=NP algorithms: Du (contradiction pairs / checking trees) wrongly rejects an infinite family of satisfiable formulas (He et al. 2024); Quigley (bounded-length clause derivation) wrongly accepts an infinite family of UNSAT formulas, and unbounded derivation grows exponentially (DeJesse, Lyudovyk, Pai 2025).

statement: EXPANSION POINT of the count identity (director's recollection; verify before citing): prod_e p_e(x) has an arithmetic circuit of size O(m) (one product of m small polynomials) - compact and cheap. The whole cost sits in ONE operation: the hypercube sum sum_{x in {0,1}^n}. So for the count identity the question 'where must the compact representation be expanded' has a precise answer - at the hypercube summation - and the open question is which variable-elimination orders keep the partial sums small for which formula structures.

statement: PB VIEW OF THE BLIND CASES - synthesis of findings already on file (owner 2026-11-19 PB question): the PB encoding x_i+x_j+x_k = 1, x in {0,1} is exact, but exactness is not cheap inference. (1) The LP relaxation is NEVER infeasible: x = 1/3 everywhere satisfies every clause (D-016h), so pure linear arithmetic over [0,1] refutes no positive 1-in-3 formula. (2) Depth-1 Chvatal-Gomory from A x = 1 alone refutes exactly the integer-infeasible formulas (D-023, integer Farkas / Hermite normal form). (3) Of the 1,350 GF(3)-blind sets at n=6 only 30 are integer-infeasible (R0100/R0101). So the cheap PB steps catch 30 of 1,350; the other 1,320 need the bounds 0 <= x <= 1 combined with deeper cuts or conflict learning - that is where the PB information difference sits.

question: WHICH PB INEQUALITIES CLOSE THE GAP (owner 2026-11-19): for the 1,320 GF(3)-blind, integer-solvable, Boolean-UNSAT sets at n=6 (and targeted n=7..9): (a) the Chvatal-Gomory rank WITH the bounds 0 <= x <= 1 (or a lift-and-project / Sherali-Adams level as exact proxy) - distribution, and which structure forces rank >= 2; (b) the smallest set of derived PB inequalities (weighted, after division/rounding) that refutes each, compared with the number of resolution steps / CDCL conflicts for the same set; (c) are there a FEW inequality TEMPLATES (e.g. odd-set / overlap-pattern cuts) that refute all of them - if so, state each template as a lemma with proof and test it on n=7..9; (d) cost of finding them (automatability), not only their size.

CLAIM: Let F be a finite CNF over n Boolean variables, with clauses interpreted as disjunctions of literals. For each clause c, let A_c be the assignments that falsify c. For every subset S of clauses, the intersection of the A_c for c in S is empty if the falsifying requirements conflict; otherwise it has size 2^(n-|V(S)|), where V(S) is the set of variables occurring in clauses in S. Consequently #SAT(F) = sum over S of (-1)^|S| times this intersection size. The empty subset contributes 2^n; tautological clauses have empty falsification events; repeated literals are allowed.

source: A. Del Pia, 'Integer programming on polytopes of Chvatal rank one is as hard as lattice problems', arXiv Oct 2026 (owner deep research 2026-11-19; not re-read by the director)
statement: Del Pia (2026-10-07): integer programming on polytopes of Chvatal rank at most 1 is as hard as lattice problems (conditional on LWE-type assumptions): short rank-1 cutting-plane refutations can exist while FINDING them is hard - necessary rank != discovery cost.

WITNESS GENERATOR from D-018 (owner 2026-11-19): adding a constant c to all coordinates keeps every clause sum mod 3 (3c = 0), and two distinct values can always be shifted onto {0,1}; a constant vector is never a solution. Hence every GF(3) solution of a BLIND formula uses all three values, and every blind formula on n variables is, up to isomorphism, a subset of the clauses allowed by a witness with value counts (k0,k1,k2), all >= 1, up to cyclic shift. n=7: 5 types, 2^10+2^10+2^12+2^13+2^11 = 16,384 candidate clause sets instead of 2^35. Upper bounds on candidates: n=6: 320, n=7: 16,384, n=8: 5,046,272, n=9: 12,519,997,440 (before dedup). Minimal-UNSAT reduction: every UNSAT formula contains an MUS; a GF(3)-inconsistent MUS has no integer solution and is refuted by one CG round (D-023); adding clauses only shrinks the first CG closure - so the maximal CG rank over all UNSAT formulas on <= n variables is attained on blind MUS classes.

source: Aaronson SIGACT News 2005 and Proc. R. Soc. A 2005; Oltean 2008; Valiant-Vazirani 1986 (director's recollection; verify before citing)
statement: Physical NP solvers and their hidden costs: linear optics driven by classical (coherent) light is classically simulable in time polynomial in the number of modes; optical 'solvers' for subset sum / Hamiltonian path move the exponential into the number of paths, delays or intensity (Oltean et al. 2008-2009); coherent Ising machines minimise QUBO energies heuristically without polynomial guarantees; reading an amplitude of size 2^-n needs exponentially many repetitions or exponential precision; PostBQP = PP (Aaronson 2005) shows postselection is such a hidden resource; Valiant-Vazirani: SAT reduces (randomised) to instances with at most one solution, so a solver cannot avoid the C = 1 case.

INTERFERENCE = GF(3) CHARACTER SUMS (director synthesis for the spatiotemporal handover): a clause test x_i + x_j + x_k = 1 (mod 3) written with phases is (1/3) sum_t omega^{t(x_i+x_j+x_k-1)}, omega = e^{2 pi i/3}. Summed over the whole group F_3^n, the interference total is 3^(n-r) or 0 - exactly GF(3) consistency, computable by linear algebra, and blind to the 1,350 sets at n=6. Restricted to the Boolean cube {0,1}^n the same phases give the exact count Z(F) - a hypercube sum (VNP form), with no group structure to exploit. So a linear wave/interference model reproduces our known dichotomy: the efficient part is GF(3), the exact part is the hypercube sum. Readout: SAT formulas with exactly one solution exist (C = 1 rows in topic_onein3), so a normalised Boolean amplitude can be 2^-n. The QUBO energy E_F(x) = sum (x_i+x_j+x_k-1)^2 is an integer, so its SAT/UNSAT gap is always >= 1 (good readout margin) - the cost then sits in reaching the minimum, i.e. in the dynamics.

question: SPATIOTEMPORAL / INTERFERENCE MODEL (owner handover 2026-11-19), hypotheses testable on our exact data: (H1) a phase-propagation model over F_3 (clause operators as phase masks, linear recombination) decides exactly cons3 - check on the 1,350 blind sets at n=6 that its observable equals the GF(3) answer, i.e. it is blind there; (H2) readout precision: on topic_onein3 measure, per n, the smallest nonzero normalised Boolean amplitude Z(F)/2^n over SAT formulas and how many unique-solution formulas exist - is the decay 2^-n (then a linear readout needs exponential precision)? (H3) the nonlinear route: for the QUBO landscape E_F on {0,1}^n compare blind vs non-blind UNSAT and SAT formulas - number of local minima, barrier heights, mixing / convergence time of a simple annealing dynamics as n grows; where does the cost of an energy-minimising machine sit? Every resource (modes, time bins, precision bits, repetitions) is counted; no exponential resource is free.

question: Q-c923363d5f
scope: Disjoint family C_n, natural order. Not a statement about cyclic or general 3-CNF families.
statement: The identity in NUMERICAL_EVIDENCE (a) holds for all n and all k. Proof sketch: for a prefix, all blocks fully inside the prefix are either satisfied (dropped) or falsified (contradiction). Blocks entirely unassigned are identical across assignments. Only the block cut by the prefix varies. For k mod 3 = 0 there is no cut block (residual count 1). For k mod 3 = 1 the cut block is satisfied (empty) or leaves a 2-clause (count 2). For k mod 3 = 2 it is satisfied or leaves a unit clause (count 2). Hence the count is crossing(k)+1 in all cases, and it is independent of n.

question: Support lemma: a GF(2)-rank-r clause set lies in the span of r independent clauses, so all its clause vectors are supported on at most 3r variables (proof: coordinates outside the union of the r basis supports vanish on the whole span). theorem sum_ones : ∀ c : List Nat, (c.map (fun _ : Nat => 1)).sum = c.length
  | [] => rfl
  | _ :: t => by
      rw [List.map_cons, List.sum_cons, List.length_cons, sum_ones t]

theorem one_in_three_gf2_solvable :
    ∀ phi : List (List Nat),
      (∀ c, c ∈ phi → c.length = 3 ∧ c.Nodup) →
      ∃ x : Nat → Nat, (∀ v, x v < 2) ∧ ∀ c, c ∈ phi → (c.map x).sum % 2 = 1 := by
  intro phi hphi
  refine ⟨fun _ => 1, fun _ => by show (1:Nat) < 2; decide, ?_⟩
  intro c hc
  have hlen : c.length = 3 := (hphi c hc).1
  show (c.map (fun _ : Nat => 1)).sum % 2 = 1
  rw [sum_ones c, hlen]

#print axioms one_in_three_gf2_solvable

Proof sketch: each clause has exactly one true variable, so the number of (clause, true variable) incidences is m, and it also equals d*|T| for the true set T. Hence d*|T| = m. The condition is necessary, not sufficient.

      ↔ (∃ a b : Nat, ∀ v, v < n → x0 v = a ∨ x0 v = b) := by
  have fin : ∀ p q : Nat, p < 3 → q < 3 → ∃ t, ∀ w, w < 3 → (w = p ∨ w = q) → (w + t) % 3 ≤ 1 := by
    intro p q hp hq

statement: Exhaustive n=6 enumeration (all 2^20 triple-sets, experiment cm-7e1dbca3747b4714): among d-regular positive 1-in-3 instances (every variable in exactly d clauses) the satisfiable and unsatisfiable counts are (d,m)=(1,2): 10 sat/0 unsat; (2,4): 75/0; (3,6): 300/30; (4,8): 285/495; (5,10): 90/954; (6,12): 15/765; (7,14): 0/330; (8,16): 0/75; (9,18): 0/10; (10,20): 0/1. Two findings. (a) Sufficiency of d | m is FALSE: the instances (3,6) and (4,8) are unsatisfiable although d divides m. (b) The necessity check 'sat implies d | m' gave 0 violations, but at n=6 every d-regular instance has m = 2d (since 6d = 3m), so d | m holds automatically and the check is vacuous. It does not test the divisibility necessity. The necessity itself is a proof (counting), so the test is only meaningful at n where n*d/3 is not a multiple of d, e.g. n=7, d=3, m=7 (Fano).

def bitAt (x : List Nat) (i : Nat) : Nat := x.getD i 0

def pc (i j k : Nat) (x : List Nat) : Int :=
  let a : Int := (bitAt x i : Int)
  let b : Int := (bitAt x j : Int)
  let c : Int := (bitAt x k : Int)
  a + b + c - 2 * (a * b + a * c + b * c) + 3 * (a * b * c)

def oneIn (i j k : Nat) (x : List Nat) : Bool :=
  (bitAt x i + bitAt x j + bitAt x k == 1)

def prodPc : List (Nat × Nat × Nat) → List Nat → Int
  | [], _ => 1
  | c :: F, x => pc c.1 c.2.1 c.2.2 x * prodPc F x

def allBits : Nat → List (List Nat)
  | 0 => [[]]
  | n + 1 => (allBits n).flatMap (fun b => [0 :: b, 1 :: b])

def closedCount (F : List (Nat × Nat × Nat)) (n : Nat) : Int :=
  ((allBits n).map (fun x => prodPc F x)).sum

def bruteCount (F : List (Nat × Nat × Nat)) (n : Nat) : Nat :=
  ((allBits n).filter (fun x => F.all (fun c => oneIn c.1 c.2.1 c.2.2 x))).length

theorem bits_le_one : ∀ (n : Nat) (x : List Nat), x ∈ allBits n → ∀ m, bitAt x m ≤ 1
  | 0, x, hx, m => by
    simp [allBits] at hx
    subst hx
    simp [bitAt]
  | n + 1, x, hx, m => by
    simp [allBits] at hx
    obtain ⟨a, ha, hx⟩ := hx
    have ih := bits_le_one n a ha
    rcases hx with rfl | rfl
    · cases m with
      | zero => simp [bitAt]
      | succ m => simpa [bitAt] using ih m
    · cases m with
      | zero => simp [bitAt]
      | succ m => simpa [bitAt] using ih m

theorem key_ind (a b c : Nat) (ha : a ≤ 1) (hb : b ≤ 1) (hc : c ≤ 1) :
    ((a : Int) + (b : Int) + (c : Int) - 2 * ((a : Int) * (b : Int) + (a : Int) * (c : Int) + (b : Int) * (c : Int)) + 3 * ((a : Int) * (b : Int) * (c : Int)))
      = if (a + b + c == 1) = true then 1 else 0 := by
  rcases (show a = 0 ∨ a = 1 by omega) with rfl | rfl <;>
  rcases (show b = 0 ∨ b = 1 by omega) with rfl | rfl <;>
  rcases (show c = 0 ∨ c = 1 by omega) with rfl | rfl <;> decide

theorem pc_eq_ind (i j k : Nat) (x : List Nat) (h : ∀ m, bitAt x m ≤ 1) :
    pc i j k x = if oneIn i j k x = true then 1 else 0 := by
  unfold pc oneIn
  exact key_ind _ _ _ (h i) (h j) (h k)

theorem prod_eq (x : List Nat) (h : ∀ m, bitAt x m ≤ 1) :
    ∀ (F : List (Nat × Nat × Nat)), prodPc F x = if F.all (fun c => oneIn c.1 c.2.1 c.2.2 x) = true then 1 else 0
  | [] => by simp [prodPc]
  | c :: F => by
    have ih := prod_eq x h F
    rw [prodPc, pc_eq_ind c.1 c.2.1 c.2.2 x h, ih]
    by_cases h1 : oneIn c.1 c.2.1 c.2.2 x = true <;> by_cases h2 : F.all (fun d => oneIn d.1 d.2.1 d.2.2 x) = true <;> simp [List.all_cons, h1, h2]

theorem closed_eq_brute_aux (F : List (Nat × Nat × Nat)) : ∀ (L : List (List Nat)), (∀ x, x ∈ L → ∀ m, bitAt x m ≤ 1) → (L.map (fun x => prodPc F x)).sum = ((L.filter (fun x => F.all (fun c => oneIn c.1 c.2.1 c.2.2 x))).length : Int)
  | [], _ => by simp
  | x :: L, h => by
    have hx : ∀ m, bitAt x m ≤ 1 := h x (by simp)
    have ih := closed_eq_brute_aux F L (fun y hy => h y (by simp [hy]))
    simp only [List.map_cons, List.sum_cons]
    rw [prod_eq x hx F, ih]
    simp only [List.filter_cons]
    by_cases h1 : F.all (fun c => oneIn c.1 c.2.1 c.2.2 x) = true <;> simp [h1] <;> omega

theorem onein3_closed_form_eq_brute (F : List (Nat × Nat × Nat)) (n : Nat) :
    closedCount F n = (bruteCount F n : Int) := by
  unfold closedCount bruteCount
  exact closed_eq_brute_aux F (allBits n) (fun x hx => bits_le_one n x hx)

def inc (e : Nat × Nat) (v : Nat) : Bool := decide (e.1 = v ∨ e.2 = v)

def cnt : Nat → (Nat → Bool) → Nat
  | 0, _ => 0
  | k + 1, p => cnt k p + (if p k = true then 1 else 0)

def occ (n : Nat) (E : Nat → Nat × Nat) (i : Nat) : Nat := cnt n (fun v => inc (E i) v)

def Sat (n m : Nat) (E : Nat → Nat × Nat) : Prop :=
  ∃ x : Nat → Bool, ∀ v, v < n → cnt m (fun i => inc (E i) v && x i) = 1

def PM (n m : Nat) (E : Nat → Nat × Nat) : Prop :=
  ∃ M : Nat → Bool, (∀ v, v < n → ∃ i, i < m ∧ inc (E i) v = true ∧ M i = true) ∧
    (∀ v, v < n → ∀ i j, i < m → j < m → inc (E i) v = true → inc (E j) v = true → M i = true → M j = true → i = j)

theorem cp (a b : Nat) (hab : a ≠ b) (k : Nat) :
    cnt k (fun v => decide (a = v ∨ b = v)) = (if a < k then 1 else 0) + (if b < k then 1 else 0) := by
  induction k with
  | zero => simp [cnt]
  | succ k ih =>
    simp only [cnt, ih, decide_eq_true_eq]
    repeat' split
    all_goals omega

theorem cnz (p : Nat → Bool) (k : Nat) : cnt k p ≠ 0 → ∃ i, i < k ∧ p i = true := by
  induction k with
  | zero => intro h; simp [cnt] at h
  | succ k ih =>
    intro h
    simp only [cnt] at h
    by_cases hk : p k = true
    · exact ⟨k, Nat.lt_succ_self k, hk⟩
    · have h0 : cnt k p ≠ 0 := by
        intro h0; apply h; simp [hk, h0]
      obtain ⟨i, hi, hpi⟩ := ih h0
      exact ⟨i, by omega, hpi⟩

theorem cpos (p : Nat → Bool) (k : Nat) : ∀ j, j < k → p j = true → 1 ≤ cnt k p := by
  induction k with
  | zero => intro j hj _; omega
  | succ k ih =>
    intro j hj hp
    simp only [cnt]
    by_cases hjk : j < k
    · have := ih j hjk hp
      omega
    · have hpk : p k = true := by
        have : j = k := by omega
        rw [← this]; exact hp
      have h1 : (if p k = true then 1 else 0) = 1 := by simp [hpk]
      omega

theorem ctwo (p : Nat → Bool) (k : Nat) : ∀ i j, i < k → j < k → i ≠ j → p i = true → p j = true → 2 ≤ cnt k p := by
  induction k with
  | zero => intro i j hi _ _ _ _; omega
  | succ k ih =>
    intro i j hi hj hij hpi hpj
    simp only [cnt]
    by_cases hik : i = k
    · have h1 := cpos p k j (by omega) hpj
      have hpk : p k = true := by rw [← hik]; exact hpi
      have h2 : (if p k = true then 1 else 0) = 1 := by simp [hpk]
      omega
    · by_cases hjk : j = k
      · have h1 := cpos p k i (by omega) hpi
        have hpk : p k = true := by rw [← hjk]; exact hpj
        have h2 : (if p k = true then 1 else 0) = 1 := by simp [hpk]
        omega
      · have h1 := ih i j (by omega) (by omega) hij hpi hpj
        omega

theorem cle (p : Nat → Bool) (k : Nat) : (∀ i j, i < k → j < k → p i = true → p j = true → i = j) → cnt k p ≤ 1 := by
  induction k with
  | zero => intro _; simp [cnt]
  | succ k ih =>
    intro hu
    simp only [cnt]
    have hc := ih (fun i j hi hj hp hq => hu i j (by omega) (by omega) hp hq)
    by_cases hpk : p k = true
    · have h0 : cnt k p = 0 := by
        by_cases hz : cnt k p = 0
        · exact hz
        · obtain ⟨i, hi, hpi⟩ := cnz p k hz
          have := hu i k (by omega) (by omega) hpi hpk
          omega
      have h1 : (if p k = true then 1 else 0) = 1 := by simp [hpk]
      omega
    · have h1 : (if p k = true then 1 else 0) = 0 := by simp [hpk]
      omega

theorem phi_occ_and_sat_iff_pm (n m : Nat) (E : Nat → Nat × Nat)
    (hloop : ∀ i, i < m → (E i).1 ≠ (E i).2 ∧ (E i).1 < n ∧ (E i).2 < n)
    (hcubic : ∀ v, v < n → cnt m (fun i => inc (E i) v) = 3) :
    (∀ i, i < m → occ n E i = 2) ∧ (Sat n m E ↔ PM n m E) := by

    have h := hloop i hi
    have hc := cp (E i).1 (E i).2 h.1 n

evidence.checked_file:
def dot : List Nat → List Nat → Nat
  | [], _ => 0
  | _ :: _, [] => 0
  | w :: ws, b :: bs => w * b + dot ws bs

def total : List Nat → Nat
  | [] => 0
  | w :: ws => w + total ws

theorem dot_le_total (w : List Nat) : ∀ (s : List Nat), (∀ b ∈ s, b ≤ 1) → dot w s ≤ total w := by
  induction w with
  | nil =>
    intro s _
    simp [dot, total]
  | cons x xs ih =>
    intro s hs
    cases s with
    | nil => simp [dot, total]
    | cons b bs =>
      have hb : b ≤ 1 := hs b (by simp)
      have hrest : ∀ c ∈ bs, c ≤ 1 := fun c hc => hs c (by simp [hc])
      have h1 : x * b ≤ x := by
        have hcase : b = 0 ∨ b = 1 := by omega
        rcases hcase with h | h <;> subst h <;> simp
      have h2 := ih bs hrest
      simp only [dot, total]
      omega

theorem subset_sum_mod_iff (w : List Nat) (t M : Nat) (ht : t ≤ total w) (hM0 : 0 < M) (hMt : t < M) (hMS : total w - t < M) : (∃ s : List Nat, s.length = w.length ∧ (∀ b ∈ s, b = 0 ∨ b = 1) ∧ dot w s % M = t % M) ↔ (∃ s : List Nat, s.length = w.length ∧ (∀ b ∈ s, b = 0 ∨ b = 1) ∧ dot w s = t) := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨s, hlen, hb, hmod⟩
    refine ⟨s, hlen, hb, ?_⟩
    have hle : dot w s ≤ total w := dot_le_total w s (fun b hb' => by rcases hb b hb' with h | h <;> omega)
    have hlt : t % M = t := Nat.mod_eq_of_lt hMt
    have hdm : dot w s % M = t := by rw [hmod, hlt]
    have key : dot w s % M + M * (dot w s / M) = dot w s := Nat.mod_add_div (dot w s) M
    rw [hdm] at key
    rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos (dot w s / M) with h0 | hpos
    · rw [h0, Nat.mul_zero] at key
      omega
    · obtain ⟨k, hk⟩ : ∃ k, dot w s / M = k + 1 := ⟨dot w s / M - 1, by omega⟩
      rw [hk, Nat.mul_add, Nat.mul_one] at key
      omega
  · rintro ⟨s, hlen, hb, heq⟩
    exact ⟨s, hlen, hb, by rw [heq]⟩

#print axioms subset_sum_mod_iff

def tbl (tt : Nat → Bool) (n m : Nat) : List Bool :=
  (List.range (2 ^ n)).map (fun a => tt (Nat.lor a m))

def popcF : Nat → Nat → Nat
  | 0, _ => 0
  | f + 1, m => m % 2 + popcF f (m / 2)

def dedupF {α : Type} [BEq α] : Nat → List α → List α
  | 0, _ => []
  | _ + 1, [] => []
  | f + 1, x :: xs => x :: dedupF f (xs.filter (fun y => !(y == x)))

def Dk (tt : Nat → Bool) (n k : Nat) : Nat :=
  (dedupF (2 ^ n) (((List.range (2 ^ n)).filter (fun m => popcF n m == k)).map (fun m => tbl tt n m))).length

theorem filt_len {α : Type} (p : α → Bool) : ∀ l : List α, (l.filter p).length ≤ l.length
  | [] => Nat.le_refl 0
  | x :: xs => by
    have ih := filt_len p xs
    simp only [List.filter]
    split <;> simp only [List.length_cons] <;> omega

theorem dedupF_len {α : Type} [BEq α] : ∀ (f : Nat) (l : List α), (dedupF f l).length ≤ l.length
  | 0, l => by simp [dedupF]
  | _ + 1, [] => by simp [dedupF]
  | f + 1, x :: xs => by
    have ih := dedupF_len f (xs.filter (fun y => !(y == x)))
    have h2 := filt_len (fun y => !(y == x)) xs
    simp only [dedupF, List.length_cons]
    omega

theorem dk_le_two_pow (tt : Nat → Bool) (n k : Nat) : Dk tt n k ≤ 2 ^ n := by
  unfold Dk
  have h1 := dedupF_len (2 ^ n) (((List.range (2 ^ n)).filter (fun m => popcF n m == k)).map (fun m => tbl tt n m))
  have h2 := filt_len (fun m => popcF n m == k) (List.range (2 ^ n))
  rw [List.length_map] at h1
  rw [List.length_range] at h2
  omega

def InRange (n j : Nat) : Prop := 1 ≤ j ∧ j ≤ n

def WF (n : Nat) (c : Nat × Nat × Nat) : Prop :=
  InRange n c.1 ∧ InRange n c.2.1 ∧ InRange n c.2.2 ∧
  c.1 ≠ c.2.1 ∧ c.1 ≠ c.2.2 ∧ c.2.1 ≠ c.2.2

def sum3 (v : Nat → Nat) (c : Nat × Nat × Nat) : Nat :=
  (v c.1 + v c.2.1 + v c.2.2) % 3

def ind (u : Nat → Nat) (j : Nat) : Nat := if u j = 1 then 1 else 0

def cnt (u : Nat → Nat) (c : Nat × Nat × Nat) : Nat :=
  ind u c.1 + ind u c.2.1 + ind u c.2.2

def SatMod3 (n : Nat) (F : List (Nat × Nat × Nat)) (v : Nat → Nat) : Prop :=
  (∀ j, InRange n j → v j < 3) ∧
  (∃ a b : Nat, a < 3 ∧ b < 3 ∧ ∀ j, InRange n j → v j = a ∨ v j = b) ∧
  ∀ c ∈ F, sum3 v c = 1

def OneInThree (n : Nat) (F : List (Nat × Nat × Nat)) (u : Nat → Nat) : Prop :=
  (∀ j, InRange n j → u j = 0 ∨ u j = 1) ∧
  ∀ c ∈ F, cnt u c = 1

theorem pnp_ind (u : Nat → Nat) (j : Nat) (h : u j = 0 ∨ u j = 1) :
    ind u j = u j := by
  unfold ind
  rcases h with h | h <;> simp [h]

theorem pnp_cnt (u : Nat → Nat) (c : Nat × Nat × Nat)
    (h1 : u c.1 = 0 ∨ u c.1 = 1) (h2 : u c.2.1 = 0 ∨ u c.2.1 = 1)
    (h3 : u c.2.2 = 0 ∨ u c.2.2 = 1) :
    cnt u c = u c.1 + u c.2.1 + u c.2.2 := by
  unfold cnt
  rw [pnp_ind u c.1 h1, pnp_ind u c.2.1 h2, pnp_ind u c.2.2 h3]

theorem pnp_key (p q r s t : Nat) (hp : p = s ∨ p = t) (hq : q = s ∨ q = t)
    (hr : r = s ∨ r = t) (hd : (t + 3 - s) % 3 = 1) (hs : (p + q + r) % 3 = 1) :
    ((p + 3 - s) % 3 = 0 ∨ (p + 3 - s) % 3 = 1) ∧
    ((q + 3 - s) % 3 = 0 ∨ (q + 3 - s) % 3 = 1) ∧
    ((r + 3 - s) % 3 = 0 ∨ (r + 3 - s) % 3 = 1) ∧
    (p + 3 - s) % 3 + (q + 3 - s) % 3 + (r + 3 - s) % 3 = 1 := by
  rcases hp with hp | hp <;> rcases hq with hq | hq <;> rcases hr with hr | hr <;>
    refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩ <;> omega

theorem pnp_shift (n : Nat) (F : List (Nat × Nat × Nat)) (v : Nat → Nat) (s t : Nat)
    (hW : ∀ c ∈ F, WF n c)
    (hval : ∀ j, InRange n j → v j = s ∨ v j = t)
    (hd : (t + 3 - s) % 3 = 1)
    (hF : ∀ c ∈ F, sum3 v c = 1) :
    OneInThree n F (fun j => (v j + 3 - s) % 3) := by
  unfold OneInThree
  constructor
  · intro j hj
    show (v j + 3 - s) % 3 = 0 ∨ (v j + 3 - s) % 3 = 1
    rcases hval j hj with h | h <;> omega
  · intro c hc
    have hW' := hW c hc
    unfold WF at hW'
    obtain ⟨hx, hy, hz, -, -, -⟩ := hW'
    have hs := hF c hc
    unfold sum3 at hs
    obtain ⟨h1, h2, h3, hsum⟩ := pnp_key (v c.1) (v c.2.1) (v c.2.2) s t
      (hval _ hx) (hval _ hy) (hval _ hz) hd hs
    rw [pnp_cnt (fun j => (v j + 3 - s) % 3) c h1 h2 h3]
    exact hsum

theorem pnp001_g0059 (n : Nat) (F : List (Nat × Nat × Nat))
    (hW : ∀ c ∈ F, WF n c) :
    (∃ v, SatMod3 n F v) ↔ (∃ u, OneInThree n F u) := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    obtain ⟨v, hv⟩ := h
    unfold SatMod3 at hv
    obtain ⟨_, ⟨a, b, ha, hb, hval⟩, hF⟩ := hv
    by_cases h1 : (b + 3 - a) % 3 = 1
    · exact ⟨fun j => (v j + 3 - a) % 3, pnp_shift n F v a b hW hval h1 hF⟩
    · by_cases h2 : (a + 3 - b) % 3 = 1
      · exact ⟨fun j => (v j + 3 - b) % 3,
          pnp_shift n F v b a hW (fun j hj => Or.comm.mp (hval j hj)) h2 hF⟩
      · have hab : a = b := by omega
        refine ⟨fun _ => 0, ?_⟩
        unfold OneInThree
        refine ⟨fun _ _ => Or.inl rfl, ?_⟩
        intro c hc
        exfalso
        have hW' := hW c hc
        unfold WF at hW'
        obtain ⟨hx, hy, hz, -, -, -⟩ := hW'
        have hs := hF c hc
        unfold sum3 at hs
        rcases hval _ hx with h3 | h3 <;> rcases hval _ hy with h4 | h4 <;>
          rcases hval _ hz with h5 | h5 <;> omega
  · intro h
    obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := h
    unfold OneInThree at hu
    obtain ⟨hu01, hC⟩ := hu
    refine ⟨u, ?_⟩
    unfold SatMod3
    refine ⟨?_, ⟨0, 1, by decide, by decide, hu01⟩, ?_⟩
    · intro j hj
      rcases hu01 j hj with h' | h' <;> omega
    · intro c hc
      have hC' := hC c hc

      unfold sum3
      omega

def clauseSum (x : Nat → Nat) (c : List Nat) : Nat := (c.map x).sum

def satisfies (F : List (List Nat)) (x : Nat → Nat) : Prop :=
  ∀ c ∈ F, clauseSum x c = 1

def solvesGF3 (F : List (List Nat)) (x : Nat → Nat) : Prop :=
  ∀ c ∈ F, clauseSum x c % 3 = 1

theorem clause_iff (x : Nat → Nat) (c : List Nat) (hl : c.length = 3)
    (hb : ∀ v ∈ c, x v = 0 ∨ x v = 1) :
    clauseSum x c % 3 = 1 ↔ clauseSum x c = 1 := by
  rcases c with _ | ⟨p, _ | ⟨q, _ | ⟨r, _ | ⟨s, t⟩⟩⟩⟩
  · simp only [List.length_cons, List.length_nil] at hl <;> omega
  · simp only [List.length_cons, List.length_nil] at hl <;> omega
  · simp only [List.length_cons, List.length_nil] at hl <;> omega
  · have hp := hb p (by simp)
    have hq := hb q (by simp)
    have hr := hb r (by simp)
    simp only [clauseSum, List.map_cons, List.map_nil, List.sum_cons, List.sum_nil]
    constructor <;> intro h <;> omega
  · simp only [List.length_cons, List.length_nil] at hl <;> omega

theorem oneinthree_gf3 (n : Nat) (F : List (List Nat)) (x : Nat → Nat)
    (hF : ∀ c ∈ F, c.length = 3 ∧ c.Nodup ∧ ∀ v ∈ c, v < n)
    (hx : ∀ j, j < n → (x j = 0 ∨ x j = 1)) :
    (solvesGF3 F x ↔ satisfies F x) := by
  constructor
  · intro h c hc
    have hc' := hF c hc
    have hb : ∀ v ∈ c, x v = 0 ∨ x v = 1 := fun v hv => hx v (hc'.2.2 v hv)
    exact (clause_iff x c hc'.1 hb).mp (h c hc)
  · intro h c hc
    have hc' := hF c hc
    have hb : ∀ v ∈ c, x v = 0 ∨ x v = 1 := fun v hv => hx v (hc'.2.2 v hv)
    exact (clause_iff x c hc'.1 hb).mpr (h c hc)

abbrev Sat1in3 (n : Nat) (F : List (Nat × Nat × Nat)) : Prop :=
  ∃ y : Nat → Nat, (∀ i, i < n → y i ≤ 1) ∧ ∀ c, c ∈ F → y c.1 + y c.2.1 + y c.2.2 = 1

abbrev Gf3Solves (n : Nat) (F : List (Nat × Nat × Nat)) (x : Nat → Nat) : Prop :=
  (∀ i, i < n → x i < 3) ∧ ∀ c, c ∈ F → (x c.1 + x c.2.1 + x c.2.2) % 3 = 1

abbrev TwoValues (n : Nat) (x : Nat → Nat) : Prop :=
  ∃ p q : Nat, p ≠ q ∧ (∀ i, i < n → x i = p ∨ x i = q) ∧ (∃ i, i < n ∧ x i = p) ∧ (∃ j, j < n ∧ x j = q)

def ind (a b : Nat) : Nat := if a = b then 1 else 0

theorem ind_le (a b : Nat) : ind a b ≤ 1 := by
  unfold ind
  split <;> omega

The right side (`∃ w` with `w v ∈ {0,1}` and every clause summing to 1 over the three distinct variables from `hdist`) is positive 1-in-3 satisfiability. statement: For every n >= 3 and every nonempty set F of distinct weight-3 clauses over variables 0..n-1: there is a GF(3) vector x with x_a+x_b+x_c = 1 (mod 3) for every clause {a,b,c} in F, taking exactly two distinct values, if and only if F has a 0/1 solution (exactly one variable equal to 1 in every clause). Proof: for distinct values a,b in GF(3) write x = a + (b-a) w with w in {0,1}^n. Then sum over a clause equals (b-a) * sum(w) mod 3, so the clause condition is sum(w) = (b-a)^{-1} = (b-a) mod 3 (sum(w) in {0,..,3}). If b-a = 1, this is 1-in-3 on w. If b-a = 2, sum(w) = 2 on every clause, i.e. sum(1-w) = 1, so 1-in-3 on z = 1-w. Both cases give a 0/1 solution of F. Conversely a 0/1 solution w gives x = w, which takes values {0,1} (exactly two values because each clause contains a 0 and a 1). Hence the set of GF(3) solutions using at most two values is nonempty exactly when F is positive 1-in-3 satisfiable.

def SolvableGF3 (F : List (List Nat)) : Prop :=
  ∃ x : Nat → Nat, (∀ v, x v < 3) ∧ ∀ c ∈ F, (c.map x).sum % 3 = 1 % 3

def Sat131 (F : List (List Nat)) : Prop :=
  ∃ a : Nat → Nat, (∀ v, a v = 0 ∨ a v = 1) ∧
    ∀ c ∈ F, (c.filter (fun v => decide (a v = 1))).length = 1

theorem one_in_three_implies_gf3 (F : List (List Nat)) (h : Sat131 F) : SolvableGF3 F := by
  obtain ⟨a, ha01, hF⟩ := h
  have key : ∀ (l : List Nat), (l.map a).sum = (l.filter (fun v => decide (a v = 1))).length := by
    intro l
    induction l with
    | nil => simp
    | cons w t ih =>
      rw [List.map_cons, List.sum_cons, ih]
      by_cases hw : a w = 1
      · simp [List.filter, hw] <;> omega
      · have h0 : a w = 0 := by
          rcases ha01 w with h1 | h1 <;> omega
        simp [List.filter, hw, h0]
  refine ⟨a, fun v => ?_, fun c hc => ?_⟩
  · rcases ha01 v with h1 | h1 <;> omega
  · rw [key c, hF c hc]

statement: For every positive 1-in-3 formula F with n variables and at least one clause (each clause a 3-subset of {0..n-1}), with A the clause incidence matrix over GF(3) and b = all-ones: F is 1-in-3 satisfiable iff the affine system A x = b over GF(3) has a solution x in GF(3)^n that takes exactly two distinct values. theorem sum_ones : ∀ C : List Nat, (C.map (fun _ => 1)).sum = C.length

    (hn : 3 ≤ n)
    (hF : ∀ C, C ∈ F → C.length = 3 ∧ C.Nodup ∧ ∀ v, v ∈ C → v < n) :

Model: branching over a FIXED variable order, exact residual-state merging via a global memo table keyed by the residual (frontier-clause state), no clause learning. (1) UNSAT invariance: on UNSAT inputs the set of computed residual states - hence W up to O(1) lookups per duplicate - is the same for DFS, BFS and every Round-Robin interleaving; it depends only on the variable order (the per-level width). (2) In-flight duplicates: under Round Robin a duplicate can arrive while its original is unfinished; then RR must wait (H > 0) or recompute (W grows) - so RR is never below DFS in this model. (3) SAT / early stop: RR over k branches has W <= k * min_i W_i (+H) (dovetailing), and there are families where a fixed DFS order needs exponentially more than RR; but some sequential order always matches RR (simulation). (4) With learning (CDCL), order changes W, but every order is bounded below by resolution size. Measure (1)-(3) on blind cores, certified n=8 cores, SAT instances and 2-SAT/XOR controls with the simulator.

statement: BRIDGE STATUS (owner 2026-11-19, literature-checked): (1) A computation trace is NOT an UNSAT proof by itself (an always-UNSAT program has short checkable traces); it becomes one only together with a proof of the algorithm s correctness. Precise known form: if the correctness of a poly-time algorithm A is provable in the bounded arithmetic PV (S^1_2), then A s UNSAT answers translate into polynomial-size Extended Frege proofs (Cook 1975; Krajicek-Pudlak). An EF lower bound would therefore exclude all poly-time algorithms with PV-provable correctness, not all algorithms. (2) Cook-Reckhow: NP = coNP iff some propositional proof system is polynomially bounded; superpolynomial lower bounds for EVERY proof system give NP != coNP (hence P != NP); a lower bound for one system (PC, EF) does not, since existence of a p-optimal proof system is open. (3) Alekseev, A lower bound for polynomial calculus with extension rule (CCC 2021 version; owner cites 2026 journal version): exponential BIT-SIZE lower bound over Q for the Binary Value Principle 1 + x1 + 2x2 + ... + 2^(n-1)xn = 0 in PC with extension variables (and radical-type rules) - bit-level/coefficient size as the measured resource, not a CNF and not over GF(2). method: affine substitution argument; formal check of (c) in the Lean lane
statement: Degree transfer from 3-colouring: for a graph G let T(G) be the positive 1-in-3 formula with clauses (x_v1,x_v2,x_v3) for every vertex v and (x_uc,x_wc,y_uwc) with a fresh variable for every edge uw and colour c. (a) T(G) is GF(3)-consistent for every G. (b) T(G) is satisfiable iff G is 3-colourable. (c) Over GF(2) modulo x^2 = x, if the XOR/carry system of T(G) (L = 1+a+b+c, q = ab+ac+bc per clause) has a polynomial-calculus refutation of degree d, then the standard 3-colouring encoding of G (sum_c x_vc = 1, x_vc x_vc' = 0, x_uc x_wc = 0) has one of degree max(d,2): substitute y_uwc := 1 + x_uc + x_wc (affine, degree-preserving); edge L maps to 0, edge q to x_uc x_wc, y^2+y to 0, vertex L to the vertex axiom, vertex q to a sum of the axioms x_vc x_vc'. CONSEQUENCE if (c) holds: the linear PC-degree lower bounds for 3-colouring of bounded-degree graphs over every field (Lauria-Nordstrom 2017) give an explicit infinite family of GF(3)-blind positive 1-in-3 formulas with PC degree Omega(n) and, by Impagliazzo-Pudlak-Sgall, PC size exp(Omega(n)) in the XOR/carry encoding over GF(2) - a class result for PC/Groebner-based procedures, not P != NP. statement: BEYOND PC (owner deep research 2026-11-19, director checks): (1) IPS TRANSFER SCHEMA: in GF(2)[x,y] (no multilinearisation) the substitution y -> 1+a+b maps L_edge to 0, q_edge to ab + (a^2+a) + (b^2+b), y^2+y to (a^2+a)+(b^2+b) (sympy-checked); vertex axioms map to colouring axioms. statement: Reduction lemma: an unused variable u in a positive 1-in-3 clause set F on n variables is free in every 0/1 and GF(3) condition. So F is GF(3)-blind with nullity k on n variables iff F restricted to the other n-1 variables is GF(3)-blind with nullity k-1 and covers them. Consequence: the kernel type of every unused-variable blind nullity-2 formula is forced to be (n-1)-1 whenever the reduced nullity-1 kernel vector has full support on the n-1 used variables. This full-support property holds for all 1,350 covering blind nullity-1 formulas at n=6 (m=4..7), which gives the 6-1 type at n=7. Whether full support is forced for all n is open.
test: Refuted if an n=7 or n=8 covering blind nullity-1 formula has a zero coordinate in its kernel vector. Test: exhaustive nullity-1 blind census at n=7 (m=5,6,7) and the n=8 sample; also check that the n=8 unused-variable rate at m=6 equals 8 times the n=7 covering nullity-1 blind count at m=6 over C(56,6) when counted exactly.

chosen_because: Prior record R0093/R0097/R0106 used exhaustive covering-only n=7 data and sampled n=8; an exhaustive census including unused-variable sets was the missing piece the question asked for. The 30-minute synchronous limit was avoided by running the census as a desk job (A0622, 52 s).

statement: LEVEL 1a monotonicity lemma. Let h(y) = SAT(F(y)), where each triple T is an input x_T that is a constant 0/1 or a single hard-input bit y_j (no negation), and F(y) = {T : x_T = 1}. Then h is monotone decreasing in y, because F(y) is monotone in y and SAT is a down-set in the triple family: if F(y') is satisfiable and F(y) is a subfamily of F(y'), then F(y) is satisfiable. Consequences: (i) MOD_q for every q >= 2 is neither monotone nor antitone, so it is not a negation-free projection of SAT or of NOT-SAT; (ii) MAJ is monotone increasing, so NOT-SAT (monotone increasing) does not exclude it by this test; (iii) the test applies to negation-free projections only, not to AC0 reductions, which may compute non-monotone gadgets before feeding SAT.
test: A finite witness: a negation-free projection P of SAT on inputs of bounded size whose output differs from MOD_q (or from its complement) at some y. The lemma predicts none exists for any q. Also check MAJ on small sizes: a projection of NOT-SAT computing MAJ_k exactly would falsify the claim that the test is vacuous for MAJ, which I do not assert.

def sumRange : Nat → (Nat → Nat) → Nat
  | 0, _ => 0
  | n+1, f => sumRange n f + f n

def inc (F : List (List Nat)) (c v : Nat) : Nat :=
  if v ∈ F.getD c [] then 1 else 0

def rowDot (F : List (List Nat)) (n : Nat) (x : Nat → Nat) (c : Nat) : Nat :=
  sumRange n (fun v => inc F c v * x v)

theorem sat_implies_cons3 (F : List (List Nat)) (n : Nat)
    (h : ∃ x : Nat → Nat, (∀ v, x v = 0 ∨ x v = 1) ∧ ∀ c, c < F.length → rowDot F n x c = 1) :
    ∃ y : Nat → Nat, ∀ c, c < F.length → rowDot F n y c % 3 = 1 := by
  obtain ⟨x, _, hx⟩ := h
  refine ⟨x, fun c hc => ?_⟩
  have := hx c hc
  omega

#print axioms sat_implies_cons3
evidence.fidelity_reason: The hypothesis (`∃ x` 0/1 with `rowDot F n x c = 1` for every clause) and conclusion (`∃ y` with `rowDot F n y c % 3 = 1`) match the claim exactly, and `∀ n` makes the variable truncation harmless. The Lean domain is broader: `F : List (List Nat)` drops the claim's "each clause is a set of exactly three distinct variables" restriction. Specialising to 3-element clauses with `n` above the largest variable index recovers the original claim, so the Lean theorem implies it.
evidence.caveat: kernel-checked Lean statement; the fidelity verdict is an independent quality control by a model, NOT a formal proof of equivalence

statement: For positive 1-in-3 formulas where every variable occurs in exactly two clauses, the clause graph is a cubic multigraph (clauses are vertices, variables are edges). The formula is SAT iff the graph has a perfect matching. By Petersen's 1891 theorem, every bridgeless cubic graph has a perfect matching, so the formula is SAT whenever the graph is bridgeless.

abbrev inS (n : Nat) (F : List (Nat × Nat × Nat)) (p : Nat → Nat) : Prop :=
  (∀ i, i < n → p i < 3) ∧ ∀ cl ∈ F, (p cl.1 + p cl.2.1 + p cl.2.2) % 3 = 1

theorem oneinthree_01_iff_not_covered (n : Nat) (F : List (Nat × Nat × Nat))
    (hF : ∀ cl ∈ F, cl.1 < n ∧ cl.2.1 < n ∧ cl.2.2 < n) :
    (∃ x : Nat → Nat, (∀ i, i < n → x i ≤ 1) ∧ ∀ cl ∈ F, x cl.1 + x cl.2.1 + x cl.2.2 = 1)
    ↔ ¬ (∀ p : Nat → Nat, inS n F p → ∃ i, i < n ∧ p i = 2) := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨x, hx01, hsum⟩ hall
    obtain ⟨i, hi, hpi⟩ := hall x ⟨fun i hi => by have := hx01 i hi; omega, fun cl hcl => by have := hsum cl hcl; omega⟩
    have := hx01 i hi
    omega
  · intro hnot
    refine Classical.byContradiction fun hno => hnot ?_
    intro p hp
    refine Classical.byContradiction fun hne => ?_
    have h01 : ∀ i, i < n → p i ≤ 1 := by
      intro i hi
      have h1 := hp.1 i hi
      have h2 : p i ≠ 2 := fun h => hne ⟨i, hi, h⟩
      omega
    exact hno ⟨p, h01, fun cl hcl => by
      obtain ⟨ha, hb, hc⟩ := hF cl hcl
      have h1 := hp.2 cl hcl
      have h2 := h01 _ ha
      have h3 := h01 _ hb
      have h4 := h01 _ hc
      omega⟩

def bits : List Nat → Prop
  | [] => True
  | x :: u => (x = 0 ∨ x = 1) ∧ bits u

def nth0 : List Nat → Nat → Nat
  | [], _ => 0
  | x :: _, 0 => x
  | _ :: u, n + 1 => nth0 u n

def dot : List Nat → List Nat → Nat
  | [], _ => 0
  | _ :: _, [] => 0
  | w :: ws, x :: u => w * x + dot ws u

theorem main_lemma : ∀ (ws : List Nat) (c : Nat) (g : List Nat → Nat),
    (∀ u : List Nat, u.length = ws.length → bits u → g u ≤ 1 ∧ g u = (c + dot ws u) % 3) →
    (∃ b, b ≤ 1 ∧ ∀ u : List Nat, u.length = ws.length → bits u → g u = b) ∨
    (∃ i, i < ws.length ∧ ((∀ u : List Nat, u.length = ws.length → bits u → g u = nth0 u i) ∨
      (∀ u : List Nat, u.length = ws.length → bits u → g u = 1 - nth0 u i))) := by
  intro ws
  induction ws with
  | nil =>
    intro c g H
    refine Or.inl ⟨g [], (H [] rfl (by simp [bits])).1, ?_⟩
    intro u hu _
    cases u with
    | nil => rfl
    | cons x v => simp at hu
  | cons w r ih =>
    intro c g H
    have key : ∀ v : List Nat, v.length = r.length → bits v →
        (g (0 :: v) ≤ 1 ∧ g (0 :: v) = (c + dot r v) % 3) ∧
        (g (1 :: v) ≤ 1 ∧ g (1 :: v) = (c + (w + dot r v)) % 3) := by
      intro v hv hb
      have h0 := H (0 :: v) (by simp [hv]) (by simp [bits, hb])
      have h1 := H (1 :: v) (by simp [hv]) (by simp [bits, hb])
      have e0 : dot (w :: r) (0 :: v) = dot r v := by simp [dot]
      have e1 : dot (w :: r) (1 :: v) = w + dot r v := by simp [dot]
      rw [e0] at h0
      rw [e1] at h1
      exact ⟨h0, h1⟩
    have hmod : w % 3 = 0 ∨ w % 3 = 1 ∨ w % 3 = 2 := by omega
    rcases hmod with hw | hw | hw
    · have hk : ∀ v : List Nat, v.length = r.length → bits v → g (0 :: v) = g (1 :: v) := by
        intro v hv hb
        obtain ⟨⟨_, b0⟩, ⟨_, b1⟩⟩ := key v hv hb
        omega
      have H' : ∀ u : List Nat, u.length = r.length → bits u →

statement: Chen-Jin-Williams, Hardness Magnification for all Sparse NP Languages, ECCC TR19-118 / FOCS 2019 (local copy literature/sources/eccc-TR19-118): if a 2^{n^{o(1)}}-sparse L in NP is not in Circuit[n^{1+eps}], then NP does not have n^k-size circuits for all k (fixed-polynomial; does NOT imply P != NP). Their intro item (1), McKay-Murray-Williams STOC 2019: if for some eps > 0 and all small beta > 0 MCSP[2^{beta m}] has no n^{1+eps}-size circuits, then NP not in P/poly.

RUNG 5 MAGNIFICATION CHECK (director 2026-11-20, report section 17): target statement = exists eps, all small beta: MCSP[2^{beta m}] has no n^{1+eps} circuits (=> NP not in P/poly => P != NP, MMW19). Proved obstacle for our tools: cut rank is not a circuit-size measure - IP_n and prod(1 + x_i y_i) have linear-size circuits but full cut rank 2^n - so all PNP-001 rank results (Lemma T, T*, M9b', Theorems 12, 14, 16) bound fixed-cut models only and cannot give superlinear general-circuit lower bounds, even before the locality barrier (CHOPRS 2020). No current PNP-001 tool addresses the rung-5 target; a new circuit-lower-bound idea is required.

Atserias-Mueller, Simple general magnification of circuit lower bounds, arXiv 2503.24061v2 (local copy literature/sources/arXiv-2503.24061): general magnification for 2^{n^{o(1)}}-sparse NP problems gives only fixed-polynomial lower bounds (Thm 4, 9; thresholds sharp); uniform magnification Thm 11: P != NP^{(+)P} if n^{-eps}-MCSP[sigma] (sigma <= 2^{o(l)}) is not in P-uniform-SIZE[n^{1+eps+o(1)}] - almost known via Santhanam-Williams and seemingly sidesteps the localization barrier; conclusion weaker than P != NP.

RUNG 5 STEP 1 (director 2026-11-20, report section 18): NEGATIVE for all current PNP-001 tools. Our lower bounds flow computation -> proofs (tiling / feasible-interpolation contrapositive: proof bounds FROM span-program bounds); the magnification target needs proofs/measures -> computation. The only formal IPS bridge (Grochow-Pitassi) reaches VP != VNP (algebraic), not Boolean P/poly; cut rank is not a circuit-size measure (sec. 17). Best partial route found: Atserias-Mueller Thm 11 (uniform, P != NP^{(+)P}, sidesteps localization) - needs uniform circuit bounds, not proof bounds. Open bridge statement: a size-s circuit for MCSP[2^{beta m}] would have to yield a small refutation of an explicit family in a system with provable lower bounds - unavailable for weak systems.

def cnt (S : Nat → Bool) (x y z : Nat) : Nat :=
  (if S x then 1 else 0) + (if S y then 1 else 0) + (if S z then 1 else 0)

theorem one_in_three_two_clauses (n : Nat) (hn : 1 ≤ n) (a b c d e f : Nat)
    (hab : a ≠ b) (hac : a ≠ c) (hbc : b ≠ c)
    (hde : d ≠ e) (hdf : d ≠ f) (hef : e ≠ f)
    (ha : a < n) (hb : b < n) (hc : c < n)
    (hd : d < n) (he : e < n) (hf : f < n) :
    ∃ S : Nat → Bool, (∀ v, S v = true → v < n) ∧
      cnt S a b c = 1 ∧ cnt S d e f = 1 := by
  by_cases h1 : a = d ∨ a = e ∨ a = f
  · refine ⟨fun v => decide (v = a), ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
    · intro v hv
      simp at hv
      omega
    · unfold cnt
      split <;> split <;> split <;> simp_all <;> omega
    · unfold cnt
      split <;> split <;> split <;> simp_all <;> omega
  · by_cases h2 : d = a ∨ d = b ∨ d = c
    · refine ⟨fun v => decide (v = d), ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
      · intro v hv
        simp at hv
        omega
      · unfold cnt
        split <;> split <;> split <;> simp_all <;> omega
      · unfold cnt
        split <;> split <;> split <;> simp_all <;> omega
    · refine ⟨fun v => decide (v = a) || decide (v = d), ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
      · intro v hv
        simp at hv
        omega
      · unfold cnt
        split <;> split <;> split <;> simp_all <;> omega
      · unfold cnt
        split <;> split <;> split <;> simp_all <;> omega

def clauseSat (x : Nat → Nat) (c : List Nat) : Prop := (c.map x).sum = 1

def formulaSat (x : Nat → Nat) (f : List (List Nat)) : Prop :=
  ∀ c, c ∈ f → clauseSat x c

theorem pnp001_g0158_one_in_three_no_sat (n u v a b c : Nat) (hn : 5 ≤ n)
    (hu : u < n) (hv : v < n) (ha : a < n) (hb : b < n) (hc : c < n)
    (huv : u ≠ v) (hua : u ≠ a) (hub : u ≠ b) (huc : u ≠ c)
    (hva : v ≠ a) (hvb : v ≠ b) (hvc : v ≠ c)
    (hab : a ≠ b) (hac : a ≠ c) (hbc : b ≠ c)
    (x : Nat → Nat) (hx : ∀ i, i < n → x i = 0 ∨ x i = 1) :
    ¬ formulaSat x [[u, v, a], [u, v, b], [u, v, c], [a, b, c]] := by
  intro h
  unfold formulaSat at h
  have h1 := h [u, v, a] (by simp)
  have h2 := h [u, v, b] (by simp)
  have h3 := h [u, v, c] (by simp)
  have h4 := h [a, b, c] (by simp)
  have bu := hx u hu
  have bv := hx v hv
  have ba := hx a ha
  have bb := hx b hb
  have bc := hx c hc
  simp [clauseSat] at h1 h2 h3 h4
  omega

On the m = n-1 cells of the sweep (n=10..14 at d=0.9, and the desk job A0805 for n=15..18), full-row-rank GF(3) systems have nullity n-m = 1, so the affine solution set of Ax=1 has exactly 3^(n-m) = 3 points. Satisfiability (a 0/1 point) is then decided by checking 3 candidates in polynomial time. These cells therefore measure a polynomially decidable family and say nothing about hardness. The exponential regime is nullity n-m growing, i.e. m/n bounded away from 1 for the question as written, or m = n - k with k growing (e.g. k ~ sqrt(n) or log n). The density question should be restated in terms of nullity k = n-m, since sat=0 at fixed k is the quantity with a 3^k enumeration cost.

Thm 3: for every oracle O and 1/2 < mu < 1, MCSP[2^{mu n}] not in BPTIME1^O[N^{1+mu'}] with queries of length N^{o(1)}. The gap to P != NP is the size parameter 2^{(1-o(1))n} vs 2^{o(n)} (authors, lines 160-165).

def clauseSum (x : Nat → Nat) : List Nat → Nat
  | [] => 0
  | v :: vs => x v + clauseSum x vs

theorem onein3_sat_implies_gf3_consistent (F : List (List Nat)) :
    (∃ x : Nat → Nat, (∀ v, x v ≤ 1) ∧ ∀ c, c ∈ F → clauseSum x c = 1) →
    (∃ y : Nat → Nat, ∀ c, c ∈ F → clauseSum y c % 3 = 1) := by
  intro h
  obtain ⟨x, _, hx⟩ := h
  refine ⟨x, ?_⟩
  intro c hc
  have h1 := hx c hc
  omega

scope: finite, n<=8, positive 1-in-3 formulas, rule set = pairwise contraction only; ZH rules beyond contraction are NOT covered
statement: SYSTEM ZH-PS (stated exactly): input D_0 = Diag(F), one tensor node per clause of a positive 1-in-3 CNF F over Boolean x (EXACT1 tensor, arity 3; diagram size linear in |F|, so no input blow-up). A ZH-PS refutation is a sequence D_0 -> ... -> D_k where each step applies one rule from a fixed finite rule set R (each rule a tensor identity valid for all values of its open wires, recognisable in polynomial time) and D_k is the scalar 0. Soundness: T(D_0) = indicator of satisfying assignments summed, so D_k = 0 with sound rules implies F unsatisfiable. (a) CONDITIONAL: if ZH-PS is polynomially bounded for all UNSAT CNFs then NP = coNP (Cook-Reckhow). It does NOT give P vs NP. (b) SUB-SYSTEM CONTRACT-PS: R restricted to pairwise contraction along shared wires (bucket/variable elimination). Its minimal refutation length under the maximum-intermediate-tensor-size measure is an exact contraction-width quantity, which is a known treewidth/branchwidth-type measure. Scope: positive 1-in-3 CNFs with n <= 8.

REDUCTION of the one-tape seed barrier (Q-5226caddf1, step 1). Set N = 2^n, machine input length N, time t = N^{1.01}, q states. Spec: Viola decomposition gives a sum of n-input ROBPs of width W = exp(O(sqrt(t)·log(tq))) (the spec's exponent is garbled; the sqrt(t) reading is the one used by Q-5226caddf1 and must be source-checked against Viola's paper). A Nisan/Forbes-Kelley-type generator for length-N ROBPs of width W has seed O~(log W) (Forbes-Kelley: O~(sqrt t)·log q here). So the seed is governed by log W, and the magnification target seed <= N^{mu'} for small mu' with t = N^{1.01} is equivalent to log W(t) <= t^{eps} for eps <= mu'/1.01. So the route needs the single lemma: a decomposition of time-t one-tape q-state DTMs into ROBPs over N input bits with log W <= t^{eps}·polylog for every eps > 0 (or for some fixed small eps). Viola's exponent 1/2 is the obstacle. Two open sub-points: (a) is log W >= Omega(t/N) (crossings per input cell) a lower bound for this decomposition, which would be harmless for t/N <= t^{eps}, i.e. only when N >= t^{1-eps}, which is not our regime N = t^{1/1.01}; (b) whether a non-ROBP generator (not via Nisan-type seeds) can beat log W. CONJECTURE, not proved. Mark as open; do not claim a route to N^{1.99} for small mu.

CORRECTION to cm-fbc4c236e94d4292 (Boolean clipped elimination matches SAT, 0 mismatches): this is Davis-Putnam variable elimination, which is sound and complete for SAT by construction. The zero-mismatch result checks the implementation only and is not evidence about rewriting completeness or proof size. The informative quantity is the maximal arity and table size of the intermediate factors (the elimination width), which is where the tensor/Boolean contraction can grow exponentially. statement: Transfer limit of the OGP -> circuit route (Q-5c20e15028). The Linial-Mansour-Nisan step needs the target Boolean function f to have Fourier weight concentrated on low degree. statement: FAST EVALUATION - independently recomputed and CONFIRMED on the stated finite domain only (not a proof of any general statement): For every positive 1-in-3 formula F with n=8 variables in the random sample of dataset agent_topic_onein3_v1_e5926cad (4000 rows with n=8, family=random), if F is GF(3)-consistent and has no Boolean (0/1) solution (gf3_blind=1; 101 such rows), then rank3(F) = 6 when m(F) = 6 and rank3(F) = 7 when m(F) in {7,8,9,10}. Here rank3 is the GF(3) rank of the clause-variable incidence matrix (rows = clauses, columns = variables) as defined in the dataset provenance, and m is the number of clauses. Also cov(F) = 8 on all 4000 rows. | scope: Finite: the 4000 n=8 random-family rows of agent_topic_onein3_v1_e5926cad (seed 20261119) and the 101 gf3_blind rows among them. No claim about n != 8, about exhaustive n=8 families, or about any general n. Only the stated rows are asserted. | evaluator: Recomputing from the raw instances on all 4000 n=8 random rows of agent_topic_onein3_v1_e5926cad: cov = 8 on every row; the 101 gf3_blind rows have rank3 = 6 for m = 6 (16 rows) and rank3 = 7 for m = 7, 8, 9, 10 (50, 20, 8, 7 rows); 0 violations, 0 mismatches against the stored columns.

question: Counterexample to hypothesis S-afb069bd09 (rank3 = min(m,7) on n=8 GF(3)-consistent, Boolean-UNSAT rows) and to claim:2f7342b5ccad: witness clauses 013,014,025,027,147,257,345 (n=8, m=7, cov=7) is GF(3)-consistent, has no Boolean 1-in-3 solution, and has GF(3) rank 6, not min(m,7)=7. The sampled census cm-013210aac49545c8 also shows rank3 is not a function of (m, cov): at m=7, cov=8 gives rank 6 (13 rows) and rank 7 (1073 rows).

chosen_because: The validator asked for a decision. The witness settles the claim as stated. The open remainder needs a new feature, not another census of the same kind.
gain: Claim-level answer: the validator's statement (rank3 = 7 for cov 7..10, and rank3 = min(m,7)) is false at n=8. Witness with cov=7, m=7, rank3=6 (cm-060e5d111fbc4ee0). cov is constant 8 in the n=8 random table, so the cov test was degenerate there. Open remainder: which invariant determines rank3 on blind n=8 rows; neither m nor cov alone does.

theorem g0170_key_gt (M L P Q : Int) (hM : 0 < M) (hP : 0 < P) (hQ0 : 0 ≤ Q) (hQ : Q < P) (hL : 0 ≤ L) :
    M * (P + Q) < (2 * M + L) * P := by
  have h1 : M * (P + Q) < M * (2 * P) := by
    first | exact Int.mul_lt_mul_of_pos_left (by omega) hM | grind
  have h2 : 0 ≤ L * P := by
    first | exact Int.mul_nonneg hL (by omega) | grind
  have h3 : (2 * M + L) * P = M * (2 * P) + L * P := by
    first | grind | simp [Int.add_mul, Int.mul_add, Int.mul_assoc, Int.mul_comm, Int.mul_left_comm]
  omega

theorem g0170_iff_key (M L P Q : Int) (hM : 0 < M) (hP : 0 < P) (hQ0 : 0 ≤ Q) :
    M * (P + Q) < (2 * M + L) * P ↔ Q * M < (M + L) * P := by
  have e1 : M * (P + Q) = M * P + M * Q := by
    first | grind | simp [Int.mul_add]
  have e2 : (2 * M + L) * P = 2 * (M * P) + L * P := by
    first | grind | simp [Int.add_mul, Int.mul_assoc]
  have e3 : (M + L) * P = M * P + L * P := by
    first | grind | simp [Int.add_mul]
  have e4 : Q * M = M * Q := by
    first | grind | exact Int.mul_comm Q M
  rw [e1, e2, e3, e4]
  constructor <;> intro h <;> omega

theorem g0170_bounded (bn bd en ed cn cd : Int) (hbd : 0 < bd) (hed : 0 < ed) (hcd : 0 < cd)
    (heta0 : 0 ≤ en) (hetab : en * bd ≤ bn * ed) (hc0 : 0 ≤ cn) (hc1 : cn < cd) :
    bd * ed * (cd + cn) < (2 * (bd * ed) + (bn * ed - en * bd)) * cd := by
  have hM : 0 < bd * ed := by
    first | exact Int.mul_pos hbd hed | grind
  have hL : 0 ≤ bn * ed - en * bd := by omega
  exact g0170_key_gt (bd * ed) (bn * ed - en * bd) cd cn hM hcd hc0 hc1 hL

theorem g0170_iff (bn bd en ed cn cd : Int) (hbd : 0 < bd) (hed : 0 < ed) (hcd : 0 < cd)

scope: Uniform random restriction, keep probability p, parity family only, finite n in 2..8. Not a claim about general formulas, the Trevisan-Xue generator, or MCSP.
statement: REFUTES S-f98d479184 in its uniform-in-p form. For parity on n variables under uniform random restriction with keep probability p, the surviving count K is Binomial(n,p) and the restricted parity has De Morgan leaf count K^2 (using the standard L(XOR_K)=K^2, Khrapchenko; this input is SOURCE, not re-verified here). Then E[L] = np(1-p) + n^2p^2, so E/(p^2 L) = 1 + (1-p)/(pn). Checked exactly for n=2..8 and p in {1/2,1/4,1/16,1/64} (e.g. n=8, p=1/64 gives 71/8). For fixed n the ratio diverges as p -> 0; at p=1/2 it is bounded by 1+1/n. Consequence: any shrinkage bound must carry a linear-in-p term or a threshold p >= c/n.

Test it on n=3 (all 256 functions, exact DP already available) and n=4 with the L>=3 restriction, then check whether the sqrt(L) term is forced or only an artifact of parity.

statement: Exact identity: in a positive 1-in-3 instance, let f = number of variables in no clause and C = the set of solutions restricted to the clause-occurring variables. The distance set of the full solution space is therefore the sumset of the core distance set with {0,...,f}, so any gap of width at most f is filled. Checked examples (owner): index/multiplexer is in THR o THR with D = 2^m but R = m; disjointness is in THR o THR with full rank 2^m for the cut x|y but at most 3 states per level in the interleaved order. def dot : List Int → List Int → Int
  | [], _ => 0
  | _ :: _, [] => 0
  | a :: r, b :: s => a * b + dot r s

abbrev IsBitVec (m : Nat) (y : List Int) : Prop :=
  y.length = m ∧ ∀ x ∈ y, x = 0 ∨ x = 1

def cube : Nat → List (List Int)
  | 0 => [[]]
  | m + 1 => (cube m).map (fun v => (0 :: v)) ++ (cube m).map (fun v => (1 :: v))

theorem cube_length : ∀ m : Nat, (cube m).length = 2 ^ m
  | 0 => by simp [cube]
  | m + 1 => by
    simp only [cube, List.length_append, List.length_map, cube_length m]
    first | omega | (rw [Nat.pow_succ, Nat.mul_two])

theorem mem_cube : ∀ (m : Nat) (y : List Int), IsBitVec m y → y ∈ cube m
  | 0, [], _ => by simp [cube]
  | 0, _ :: _, h => by
    obtain ⟨hl, _⟩ := h
    simp at hl
  | m + 1, [], h => by
    obtain ⟨hl, _⟩ := h
    exact absurd hl (by simp only [List.length_nil]; omega)
  | m + 1, x :: ys, h => by
    obtain ⟨hl, hb⟩ := h
    have hlen' : ys.length = m := by
      simp only [List.length_cons] at hl
      omega
    have hys : IsBitVec m ys := ⟨hlen', fun z hz => hb z (List.mem_cons_of_mem _ hz)⟩
    have hx : x = 0 ∨ x = 1 := hb x (by simp)
    show x :: ys ∈ (cube m).map (fun v => (0 :: v)) ++ (cube m).map (fun v => (1 :: v))
    rcases hx with rfl | rfl
    · exact List.mem_append.mpr (Or.inl (List.mem_map.mpr ⟨ys, mem_cube m ys hys, rfl⟩))
    · exact List.mem_append.mpr (Or.inr (List.mem_map.mpr ⟨ys, mem_cube m ys hys, rfl⟩))

theorem dot_bound (B : Int) (hB0 : 0 ≤ B) : ∀ (a b : List Int),
    (∀ x ∈ a, -B ≤ x ∧ x ≤ B) → (∀ x ∈ b, x = 0 ∨ x = 1) →
    -(B * (a.length : Int)) ≤ dot a b ∧ dot a b ≤ B * (a.length : Int)
  | [], b, _, _ => by simp [dot]
  | a :: r, [], ha, _ => by
    have hnn : (0:Int) ≤ ((a :: r).length : Int) := by omega
    have hdot : dot (a :: r) [] = 0 := by first | rfl | simp [dot]
    rw [hdot]
    have hk := Int.mul_nonneg hB0 hnn
    constructor <;> omega
  | a :: r, b :: s, ha, hb => by
    obtain ⟨hab1, hab2⟩ := ha a (by simp)
    have hbb := hb b (by simp)
    have ih := dot_bound B hB0 r s (fun x hx => ha x (by simp [hx])) (fun x hx => hb x (by simp [hx]))
    have hprod : -B ≤ a * b ∧ a * b ≤ B := by
      rcases hbb with h | h
      · subst h
        rw [Int.mul_zero]
        constructor <;> omega
      · subst h
        rw [Int.mul_one]
        exact ⟨hab1, hab2⟩
    have hdot : dot (a :: r) (b :: s) = a * b + dot r s := by first | rfl | simp [dot]
    have hl : ((a :: r).length : Int) = (r.length : Int) + 1 := by
      simp only [List.length_cons]
      omega
    have hexp : B * ((r.length : Int) + 1) = B * (r.length : Int) + B := by
      first | rw [Int.mul_add, Int.mul_one] | simp [Int.mul_add]
    rw [hdot, hl, hexp]
    obtain ⟨ih1, ih2⟩ := ih
    obtain ⟨hp1, hp2⟩ := hprod
    constructor <;> omega

abbrev AtMostDistinct (k l m : Nat) (F : List Int → List Int → Bool) : Prop :=
  ∃ L : List (List Int → Bool), L.length ≤ k ∧
    ∀ ρ : List Int, IsBitVec l ρ → ∃ g ∈ L, ∀ y : List Int, IsBitVec m y → F ρ y = g y

theorem atMost_pow (l m : Nat) (F : List Int → List Int → Bool) : AtMostDistinct (2^l) l m F := by
  refine ⟨(cube l).map F, ?_, ?_⟩
  · simp [cube_length]
  · intro ρ hρ
    exact ⟨F ρ, List.mem_map.mpr ⟨ρ, mem_cube l ρ hρ, rfl⟩, fun y _ => rfl⟩

theorem atMost_lin (l m : Nat) (w : List Int) (t : Int) (P : Nat)
    (hP : ∀ ρ : List Int, IsBitVec l ρ →
      -(P:Int) ≤ dot (w.take l) ρ ∧ dot (w.take l) ρ ≤ (P:Int)) :
    AtMostDistinct (2*P+1) l m
      (fun ρ y => decide (t - dot (w.take l) ρ ≤ dot (w.drop l) y)) := by
  refine ⟨(List.range (2*P+1)).map (fun i : Nat => fun y : List Int =>
      decide (t - (P:Int) + (i:Int) ≤ dot (w.drop l) y)), ?_, ?_⟩
  · simp
  · intro ρ hρ
    obtain ⟨h1, h2⟩ := hP ρ hρ
    have hnn : (0:Int) ≤ (P:Int) - dot (w.take l) ρ := by omega
    obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ : ∃ i : Nat, (i:Int) = (P:Int) - dot (w.take l) ρ := by
      first
        | exact ⟨_, (Int.toNat_of_nonneg hnn).symm⟩
        | exact (Int.eq_ofNat_of_zero_le hnn).imp fun i h => h.symm
    have hi_lt : i < 2*P+1 := by omega
    refine ⟨fun y => decide (t - (P:Int) + (i:Int) ≤ dot (w.drop l) y),
      List.mem_map.mpr ⟨i, List.mem_range.mpr hi_lt, rfl⟩, ?_⟩
    intro y _
    have hs : t - (P:Int) + (i:Int) = t - dot (w.take l) ρ := by omega
    show decide (t - dot (w.take l) ρ ≤ dot (w.drop l) y) = decide (t - (P:Int) + (i:Int) ≤ dot (w.drop l) y)
    rw [hs]

theorem atMost_min (k1 k2 l m : Nat) (F : List Int → List Int → Bool)
    (h1 : AtMostDistinct k1 l m F) (h2 : AtMostDistinct k2 l m F) :
    AtMostDistinct (min k1 k2) l m F := by
  by_cases h : k1 ≤ k2
  · rw [Nat.min_eq_left h]
    exact h1
  · rw [Nat.min_eq_right (show k2 ≤ k1 by omega)]
    exact h2

theorem pnp001_g0173_threshold_restriction_count (n : Nat) (hn : 1 ≤ n)
    (w : List Int) (hw : w.length = n) (B : Nat)
    (hB : ∀ x ∈ w, -(B:Int) ≤ x ∧ x ≤ (B:Int))
    (t : Int) (l : Nat) (hl : l ≤ n) :
    AtMostDistinct (min (2^l) (2*(l*B)+1)) l (n - l)
      (fun ρ y => decide (t - dot (w.take l) ρ ≤ dot (w.drop l) y)) := by
  have hlen : (w.take l).length = l := by
    rw [List.length_take, hw, Nat.min_eq_left hl]
  have hpre : ∀ x ∈ w.take l, -(B:Int) ≤ x ∧ x ≤ (B:Int) := by
    intro x hx
    exact hB x (by first | exact List.mem_of_mem_take hx | exact (List.take_subset _ _) hx)
  have hP : ∀ ρ : List Int, IsBitVec l ρ →
      -((l*B : Nat) : Int) ≤ dot (w.take l) ρ ∧ dot (w.take l) ρ ≤ ((l*B : Nat) : Int) := by
    intro ρ hρ
    obtain ⟨_, hbits⟩ := hρ
    have hd := dot_bound (B:Int) (by omega) (w.take l) ρ hpre (fun x hx => hbits x hx)
    rw [hlen] at hd
    have hc : ((l*B : Nat) : Int) = (B:Int) * (l:Int) := by
      first | (push_cast; exact Int.mul_comm _ _) | simp [Int.mul_comm]
    rw [hc]
    exact hd
  exact atMost_min _ _ l (n-l) _ (atMost_pow l (n-l) _) (atMost_lin l (n-l) w t (l*B) hP)

statement: Majority gate MAJ_n(x) = [sum x_i >= n/2] (fixed threshold t = n/2, unit weights) under the random restriction R_p: P[restricted gate non-constant] = 0.9654 (n=16), 0.9986 (n=36), 0.99998 (n=64), 0.9999999 (n=100) at p=1/2; and 0.6829 (n=16), 0.68274 (n=36), 0.68270 (n=64), 0.68270 (n=100) at p=1/sqrt(n). The p=1/2 values tend to 1, and the p=1/sqrt(n) values stay near 0.6827, close to P(|Z|<=1)=erf(1/sqrt2)=0.682689. So for a fixed (worst-case) threshold, the undecided fraction does not shrink with n at p=1/sqrt(n).

question: Q-23b6083e38
statement: For MAJ_n with fixed threshold t = floor(n/2) and free-variable probability p = 1/sqrt(n), the undecided probability converges to P(|Z| <= 1) = erf(1/sqrt 2) ~ 0.682689 as n -> infinity. Mechanism: the number of free variables is about Poisson(sqrt n), the fixed-part sum has spread about sqrt(n)/2, and the window has width of order the free count, so the ratio is of order 1. More generally, for worst-case thresholds the undecided probability is of order min(1, p sqrt(nz)) for weights bounded by M, which matches the bound p M sqrt(nz) of Theorem C.
test: Exact computation of the same probability for n in {200, 400, 800} (or a Gaussian approximation with an error bound). Refuted if the limit differs from erf(1/sqrt 2) by more than the observed O(1/sqrt n) correction, or if the probability at p = c/sqrt(n) depends on n for c fixed.

The conditional theorem (real polynomial with |P-H| <= eps on reachable patterns, bounded degree / monomials / coefficients -> geometric summation) stays correct. OPEN STEP: turn a probabilistic, sign-based or reachable-pattern-restricted representation of the top function into an EFFICIENTLY SUMMABLE one with numerical correctness, a certified error (e.g. E_x |P(h(x)) - H(h(x))| <= eps, certified without enumeration) and the full running time. Correction of the R0811 objection ('small-entry factorization fails for generic rank-r matrices', cm-dd4f20c35a884ed4): that objection targets factorizations W = C A with both factors small. The rank-r DP does not need that. Take r linearly independent rows of W as A = W_R. Then every row of W is W_j = C_j^T A with rational C_j, and A has entries bounded by B because it is a submatrix of W. The key vector y = Ax lies in Z^r with coordinates in [-nB, nB], so the DP has at most (2nB+1)^r states and is exact (the claim is checked on the fresh-seed recheck cm-b521a30256c947df). Extend the +-1 random-restriction lemma (P[undecided] <= 3 sqrt(2) p sqrt(n)) to bounded integer weights |w_i| <= B. scope: K2-K6 lane, Valiant depth reduction, question Q-f5792532e4
statement: Valiant's depth-reduction lemma (primary form: remove r*m/log2(d) edges to reach depth d/2^r) implies that reducing a circuit of size m = Θ(n) and depth d = N^γ to depth N^γ' requires removing a fraction (γ-γ')/γ of all wires. This is feasible (fraction < 1) iff γ' > 0. Reducing polylog depth to O(1) requires removing all wires (fraction → 1), hence is impossible. The spec's form (k*m/log2(d), depth d/2^(k-1)) with spec's k = r+1 is an equivalent restatement.
test: Check that no published application of Valiant's lemma claims polylog → O(1) depth reduction; all such applications must use a different lemma (e.g., Valiant's depth-3 reduction) or a different model.

    {X Z : Type} {k : Nat} (hk : 1 ≤ k)

bingo.name: inclusion-exclusion over falsified clause sets
bingo.preconditions: CNF F on n Boolean variables with m clauses; each clause a set of signed literals (variable, sign)
bingo.effect: #F = sum over S subset of clauses of (-1)^|S| * 2^(n-|V(S)|) * [S consistent]; S consistent iff no variable is forced to both values by the literals of S
bingo.limitations: 2^m terms, exponential in m; a counting identity, not a polynomial algorithm; yields no lower bound by itself
bingo.correctness: [x satisfies F] = prod over clauses C of (1 - [x falsifies C]); expand the product and sum over x in {0,1}^n. A product of falsification indicators over S is 1 exactly on assignments falsifying every clause of S, which exist iff S is consistent, and then fix |V(S)| variables. Verified by cm-b4aa92c386b14b14 (400 random CNFs, 0 mismatches; VERIFICATION, own code).
bingo.representations: clause sets as lists of signed literals; consistency = no variable forced to both values
bingo.interfaces: input: any clause-set representation; output: signed integer sum, groupable by a variable cut (see S-fa5d8faae8, still unverified)
bingo.provenance: S-54f648a904 (formerly UNVERIFIED_STEP, now checked by cm-b4aa92c386b14b14); recorded in session R1365 for Q-7d033113a3

bingo.name: rank-product bound for entrywise (Hadamard) product of matrices
bingo.preconditions: two matrices A, B of equal size a x b over a field F (GF(p) or any field)
bingo.effect: rank(A o B) <= rank(A) * rank(B); applied to cut matrices, the cut rank of a pointwise product of two functions is at most the product of their cut ranks
bingo.limitations: the bound is the product, not the max (max is refuted by finite data); classical Schur-product inequality, so the mechanism is a reproduction, not a new result; the bound can be far from tight and gives no lower bound; the tensor-train extension (S-c04b3d909c) is only as strong as its cut-rank = TT-rank identity, which is still unverified
bingo.correctness: rank factorisation A = U V^T, B = X Y^T; (A o B) = sum_{k,l} (U_k o X_l)(V_k o Y_l)^T, a sum of rA*rB rank-one matrices
bingo.representations: matrices over a field; rank via Gaussian elimination mod p
bingo.interfaces: input: two equal-size matrices or two functions with cut matrices; output: integer upper bound on rank of the entrywise product; composes with cut-rank / tensor-train minimisation lemmas (S-fa5d8faae8, S-6ce27138d2)
bingo.provenance: S-c04b3d909c (UNVERIFIED_STEP, matrix core now checked); verification cm-0114904a9c1e4f47 (own code, 3000 random pairs per p in {2,3,5}, 0 product-bound violations)
