statement: Correction to my previous CONNECTION record (S-a711679438). The decision-to-search step (b) was argued by checking a search circuit's output against the table; that argument is not needed. Direction needed: a search-MCSP solver of size Õ(N) and depth Õ(1) has a flag output bit (1 iff some circuit of size <= s exists). That bit is a decision circuit with the same size and depth. So a lower bound 'no decision circuit of size N(log N)^k for any depth' implies 'search-MCSP[m^c] lacks Õ(N)-size, Õ(1)-depth circuits' for the fixed k. This is EXPLORATION-level reasoning, not a verified lemma. Still open: (a) whether MMW's 'lacks' means for all sufficiently large n or infinitely many n, (b) whether MMW's oracle A can be the empty oracle (A in PH is trivially allowed), (c) the exact search output convention in MMW. H1 remains a conditional hypothesis, not a known result; nothing here claims P != NP.

statement: Dispute K11-D5, resolved on the H2 point by source. OPEN: H1 itself (a general-circuit decision lower bound for MCSP[m^c] at N*(log N)^k, infinitely often) is unproved and is the only remaining obligation; see Q-10bbdfaf2a and Q-f1e058b72f. candidate.definitions: G[K_2] = lexicographic product of G with K_2; vertices (v,i) for v∈V(G), i∈{0,1}; (a,i)~(b,j) iff a~b or (a=b and i≠j).
candidate.known_closest: The general identity tw(G[K_n]) = n(tw(G)+1)−1 for lexicographic products with cliques K_n is stated in the literature (e.g., Bodlaender 1998) but not verified for K_2.
candidate.novelty: Provides a bramble-based constructive proof for the lower bound tw(G[K_2]) ≥ 2·tw(G)+1 and combines it with the standard doubling-bag upper bound to establish exact equality.
candidate.obstacle: Verify that the family {B×{i} : B∈𝔅, i∈{0,1}} satisfies the bramble conditions (connectedness, touching) in H and that any hitting set X must have size at least 2(tw(G)+1) for arbitrary G.
candidate.attack: Check the bramble conditions on arbitrary G by constructing the family and proving the hitting-set lower bound; also verify the upper bound via the doubling-bag construction.
candidate.target_relevance: Closes the lower-bound part of the width-theorem obligation S0018, which requires proving tw(G[K_2]) ≥ 2·tw(G)+1 for all G.
candidate.derivation: 1. Let 𝔅 be a bramble of G of order q = tw(G)+1 (Seymour-Thomas). 2. In H = G[K_2] the set {B×{i} : B∈𝔅, i∈{0,1}} is connected because each B×{i} induces a copy of G[B]. 3. If B and B' touch in G, then B×{i} and B'×{j} share a vertex or have an edge in H, and B×{0} and B×{1} are adjacent via edges (a,0)-(a,1). 4. Any hitting set X of this family must satisfy |X_i| ≥ q for each i, hence |X| ≥ 2q, so the bramble order is at least 2q and tw(H) ≥ 2q-1 = 2·tw(G)+1. 5. The standard doubling-bag upper bound replaces each bag X_t by X_t×{0,1}, yielding width 2·tw(G)+1. Hence tw(G[K_2]) = 2·tw(G)+1 exactly.

MMW19 Thm 1.2 gives, for every oracle A and time-constructible s(n) >= n, a one-pass streaming algorithm for search-MCSP^A[s] with worst-case update time O~(s^2), space O~(s), and Sigma3SAT^A oracle (proof of Sec. 4: O(t) calls of length O~(t) between consecutive bits, t = Theta(s log s)). The n-dependent oracle B_n of Thm 4.1 is a separate linear-time construction and is NOT needed for Thm 1.3; my earlier 'gap (a)' was a misreading and is withdrawn. The amortised-vs-worst-case point is also moot, since Thm 1.2 already states worst-case update time. OPEN OBLIGATION (unchanged, not progress): Thm 1.3 needs the HYPOTHESIS, a fixed A in PH with no poly(s)-space, poly(s)-update-time streaming algorithm for search-MCSP^A[s]. Thm 1.2 supplies an upper bound only; the hypothesis is a lower bound and remains unproved. Scope: source reading of MMW19 Thm 1.2 and Sec. 4-5 proofs; no new theorem.

statement: Thm 4.1, Thm 5.4, Cor 6.2 of the owner's paper (as stated there). PAPER SETTING: G=(V,E) finite graph, F field, K subspace of F^I, blocks I_v; pi_X: K -> prod_{v in X} F^{I_v}. (R) rank pi_X >= d|X| for all X subset V; (L) z,z' in K with z|v != 0 != z'|v => supp z cap supp z' != empty; (E) uv in E, z|u != 0, z'|v != 0 => supports intersect. THM 4.1: R+L+E => for every finite spanning family B of K there is an injection V x [d] -> J mapping every edge of G[K_d] to an edge of the support-overlap graph H_B (adjacent iff supports intersect); spanning if dim K = d|V| and B a basis. Proof: S_v={j: b_j|v != 0} are cliques (L), S_u cup S_v cliques (E), Hall from (R). THM 5.4: colouring kernel K_G(F) = {z in F^{(VxC) u (ExC)}: sum_c z_{v,c}=0, z_{u,c}+z_{v,c}+z_{e,c}=0}, blocks {v}xC, d=2: G[K_2] subset H_B for every field and every spanning family. COR 6.2: min_B tw(H_B) = 2tw(G)+1. PAPER'S OWN LIMITS: Remark 6.4 - a parameter statement, NOT a running-time lower bound; Prop 6.5 - K_n has min overlap tw 2n-1 but constant-size Resolution refutations, so width alone gives no lower bound; Prop 5.5 - for q>=4 colours (L) fails and the analogue is false. Lean (F3 only) covers Cor 6.3 and the lower bound, NOT Thm 4.1 / Thm 5.4 as subgraph statements.

question: CAND-A quantifier check of (40a), spec v0.25 section 8.1 (page 8 read). (Q1) (40a) is written as 'for all M in M^unif_{s,A}, for all c,d, for all m0, exists m>=m0: S_M(m)>s(m)^c or tau_M(m)>s(m)^d'. This is the correct negation shape for 'infinitely often' failure of every uniform machine, and it is ALSO the form Prop 13 needs. But the box FIXES s and A only in the sentence before it ('for some admissible s,A'); the existential over (s,A) is not in the box, so the statement is 'exists s,A: (40a)'. CORRECT as a premise only with an explicit 'exists s,A in PH admissible' prefix. (Q2) The class M^unif uses 'the same output and oracle conventions as in [4]'. MMW Thm 1.2 (per the ledger, Sigma3SAT^A oracle streaming with O~(s), O~(s^2)) means that if M may query the oracle, the premise is FALSE outright. So (40a) must range over ORACLE-FREE uniform machines (A only inside the synthesized circuits). WRONG as written; corrected reading: M^unif = uniform one-pass machines with no oracle access to A. (Q3) Negation of (40a) = exists M, c, d such that for all large m, S_M(m)<=s(m)^c and tau_M(m)<=s(m)^d. This is 'eventually', not 'infinitely often'. Strength of (40a) is therefore 'for infinitely many m' (the weaker, i.e. easier-to-satisfy-the-negation side); check which one Prop 13 needs. (Q4) (8) => (40a): the exponent change c,d -> c',d' is harmless (the box is quantified over all c,d). a.e. vs i.o. is the point to check against the proof of (40). (Q5) S_M, tau_M worst case over all 2^m-bit inputs including the final report: not stated in the text; needs a definition. OPEN: whether P=NP yields an oracle-free uniform one-pass machine with S<=s^c and tau<=s^d at every large m. The natural route (store the truth table) costs 2^m space, not s^c; the MMW route needs the oracle. Prop 13's chain is therefore not verified as written.

def CycSat (n : Nat) : Prop :=
  ∃ a : Nat → Nat, (∀ j, j < n → a j ≤ 1) ∧ ∀ i, i < n → a (i % n) + a ((i + 1) % n) + a ((i + 2) % n) = 1

theorem cyc13_sat_iff_three_dvd (n : Nat) (hn : 3 ≤ n) : CycSat n ↔ 3 ∣ n := by
  unfold CycSat
  constructor
  · intro h
    obtain ⟨a, ha01, hsum⟩ := h
    apply Classical.byContradiction
    intro hnd
    have hpos : 0 < n := by omega
    have hall : ∀ m, a (m % n) + a ((m + 1) % n) + a ((m + 2) % n) = 1 := by
      intro m
      have := hsum (m % n) (Nat.mod_lt _ hpos)
      simp only [Nat.mod_mod, Nat.mod_add_mod] at this
      exact this
    have hper : ∀ x, a ((x + 3) % n) = a (x % n) := by
      intro x
      have h0 := hall x
      have h1 := hall (x + 1)
      rw [show x + 1 + 1 = x + 2 by omega, show x + 1 + 2 = x + 3 by omega] at h1
      omega
    have hstep : ∀ m, a ((m + 1) % n) = a (m % n) := by
      intro m
      have hshift : ∀ k, a ((m + 3 * k) % n) = a (m % n) := by
        intro k
        induction k with
        | zero => simp
        | succ k ih =>
          rw [show m + 3 * (k + 1) = (m + 3 * k) + 3 by omega, hper, ih]
      obtain ⟨k, t, hkt⟩ : ∃ k t : Nat, 3 * k = 1 + t * n := by
        have h3 : n % 3 = 1 ∨ n % 3 = 2 := by omega
        rcases h3 with h | h
        · exact ⟨2 * (n / 3) + 1, 2, by omega⟩
        · exact ⟨n / 3 + 1, 1, by omega⟩
      have e : (m + 3 * k) % n = (m + 1) % n := by
        rw [show m + 3 * k = (m + 1) + t * n by omega, Nat.add_mul_mod_self_right]
      rw [← e]
      exact hshift k
    have hc : ∀ j, a (j % n) = a (0 % n) := by
      intro j
      induction j with
      | zero => rfl
      | succ j ih => exact (hstep j).trans ih
    have h0 := hall 0
    have e1 := hc (0 + 1)
    have e2 := hc (0 + 2)
    omega
  · intro hd
    refine ⟨fun j => if j % 3 = 0 then 1 else 0, ?_, ?_⟩
    · intro j _
      dsimp only
      split <;> omega
    · intro i _
      simp only [Nat.mod_mod_of_dvd _ hd]
      split <;> split <;> split <;> omega

text: UNREVIEWED LEMMA (author family claude-haiku, same as this session; needs review by another model family before any use as a premise). STATEMENT: G a graph, c: V->{0,1} with sum_v c(v) even. T(G,c) is the CNF with, for each vertex v, one clause per local edge-assignment at v of parity != c(v); clause width = deg v. Let m = min{deg v : c(v)=1}. CLAIM: every resolution refutation of T(G,c) contains an initial clause of width >= m. PROOF: let x be the all-zero edge assignment. The clause at v forbids a local assignment of parity 0 when c(v)=1, so x falsifies it; x falsifies a clause only if c(v)=1, and then its width is deg v >= m. Suppose every initial clause of a refutation P has width < m. Then x satisfies every initial clause of P. Resolution preserves satisfaction by the fixed assignment x: if x satisfies C or y and D or not-y, then x satisfies C or D (if x(y)=1 it satisfies D, otherwise C). So x satisfies every clause of P, including the empty clause, a contradiction. SCOPE: GF(2) Tseitin CNF only; width only, no size bound. For G=K_n and c = indicator of one vertex, m = n-1. NOT claimed as new: this is a standard one-sided width argument for Tseitin formulas. CONSISTENCY: measured minima K3=2, K4=4, K5>=7 (cm-88c97aad7b8449b6, cm-235f5acd28484ce4) satisfy the bound. It says nothing about the GF(3) kernel encoding F(K_n) of Q-33e33ccf08, and it closes no named obligation (G0001, G0005 untouched). S0003 and S0004 remain CLAIMED.

The proof uses counting of circuits in the unrelativized world; it does not relativize (an oracle could add circuits to Y_s, changing the count). (2) Natural? The measure is space S of a linear F_2 streaming algorithm. A natural property in RR sense would be a property of the function's truth table decidable in poly(N) time that is large and constructive. Space complexity of a specific restricted model is a syntactic property of the algorithm, not a semantic property of the function. It is NOT natural in the RR sense. (3) Algebrizing? The proof is combinatorial (counting), not algebraic. (4) Localizing? The proof uses global counting over the whole kernel, not local properties. (5) Perfect-matching control: Perfect matching is in P. Does it have a linear F_2 streaming algorithm with sublinear space? Unknown, but even if it does, this bound is for search-MCSP specifically, not for all functions in P. The bound does NOT transfer to general circuits because the model is explicitly restricted to linear F_2 updates. This is a RESTRICTED MODEL lower bound, not a general circuit lower bound.
test: Check if perfect matching has a linear F_2 streaming algorithm with o(N) space. If yes, the restricted model contains a P function, so the barrier control passes (the bound correctly does not apply to that function in this model).

question: Why the stage decomposition in S0016/S0017 is forced: a single unrolled circuit for the whole run has T = N*u steps, but each step must select the input bit at the RAM's read counter, which costs N per step (N-way multiplexer over x), giving N^2*u*poly(S*w), not N*u*poly(S*w). Only a stage whose input bit x_{i+1} is a fixed wire avoids the N-way selection. So Lemma 12 (Gamma <= 2^m*poly(s)) needs a fixed stage per read with size independent of x. Under only the amortised premise sum_i t_i(x) <= N*u, the per-stage size must be max_x t_i(x), which can be N*u for one i, giving N^2*u. Candidate repair (carry a backlog of unfinished steps into the next stage) fails: a stage that stalls must hand forward a pending read bit x_j that is consumed later, so the carried state is a queue of input bits, breaking the poly(S*w) state bound. Open: whether the backlog stays bounded under sum_i t_i <= N*u with t_i >= 1 (each read takes at least one step). If the backlog is O(1) per stage, the repair works; if not, it fails. The primary-text definition of update time (G0002) decides which premise MMW Thm 1.2 gives.

question: Q-10bbdfaf2a

Backlog repair for the stage decomposition of S0016/S0017 fails. Counterexample (hand argument, N = 2^m, u >= 2): t_1(x) = N*u/2 and t_i(x) = 1 for 2 <= i <= N-1, so sum_i t_i = N*u/2 + N - 1 <= N*u. Carrying unfinished interval-1 steps forward spreads them over stages 1..N/2, each stage running u steps with no input read. Bit x_j arrives in stage j (its fixed wire) but is consumed only after interval 1 ends, around stage N/2. So about N/2 input bits are pending at the same stage, and the carried state is Theta(N) bits, not poly(S*w). The backlog is therefore not O(1) under t_i >= 1 and sum_i t_i <= N*u, which answers the open question from the previous turn negatively. Consequence: under the amortised reading of MMW Thm 1.2 (sum_i t_i <= N*u), neither the per-stage repair S0016(a) nor the backlog repair gives Lemma 12 (Gamma <= 2^m*poly(s)). Lemma 12 needs the per-interval worst-case reading, so G0002 stays the decisive gap. Not checked by the lab; no cross-family review; no verdict recorded.

namespace PNP001
def ttEval (t : Fin 16) (x y : Bool) : Bool :=
  t.val.testBit (2 * x.toNat + y.toNat)
abbrev Wire (n : Nat) := Fin n ⊕ Nat
structure Circuit (n : Nat) where
  gates : List (Fin 16 × Wire n × Wire n)
  out : Wire n
def wireVal {n : Nat} (a : Fin n → Bool) (vals : List Bool) : Wire n → Bool
  | .inl i => a i
  | .inr k => vals.getD k false
def runGates {n : Nat} (a : Fin n → Bool) :
    List (Fin 16 × Wire n × Wire n) → List Bool → List Bool
  | [], vals => vals
  | (t, l, r) :: gs, vals => runGates a gs (vals ++ [ttEval t (wireVal a vals l) (wireVal a vals r)])
def Circuit.eval {n : Nat} (C : Circuit n) (a : Fin n → Bool) : Bool :=
  wireVal a (runGates a C.gates []) C.out
def Circuit.size {n : Nat} (C : Circuit n) : Nat := C.gates.length
def Computes {n : Nat} (C : Circuit n) (f : (Fin n → Bool) → Bool) : Prop :=
  ∀ a, C.eval a = f a
def gAndNot : Circuit 2 where
  gates := [(4, Sum.inl (0 : Fin 2), Sum.inl (1 : Fin 2))]
  out := Sum.inr 0
theorem gAndNot_size : gAndNot.size = 1 := rfl
theorem gAndNot_computes : Computes gAndNot (fun a => a 0 && !a 1) := by
  intro a
  have h : ∀ x y : Bool, ttEval 4 x y = (x && !y) := by decide
  simp [Circuit.eval, gAndNot, runGates, wireVal, h]
theorem D1_refuted :
    (∃ C : Circuit 2, C.size = 1 ∧ Computes C (fun a => a 0 && !a 1)) ∧
    ¬ ∃ C' : Circuit 2, C'.size ≤ 0 ∧ Computes C' (fun a => !a 1) := by
  refine ⟨⟨gAndNot, gAndNot_size, gAndNot_computes⟩, ?_⟩
  rintro ⟨⟨gs, out⟩, hs, hc⟩
  have hg : gs = [] := List.eq_nil_of_length_eq_zero (Nat.le_zero.mp hs)
  subst hg
  unfold Computes at hc
  have h2 := hc (fun _ => false)
  cases out <;> simp [Circuit.eval, runGates, wireVal] at h2
end PNP001

**Observation:** For every finite graph \(G\) and integer \(d\ge1\),
\[
\operatorname{tw}(G[K_d])=d(\operatorname{tw}(G)+1)-1.
\]
The upper bound follows by replacing each bag \(X\) in a tree decomposition of \(G\) with \(X\times[d]\). For the lower bound, in any decomposition of \(G[K_d]\), the subtrees for the \(d\) copies of each vertex pairwise intersect. Subtree Helly gives a common intersection for each vertex. Those intersections form a tree decomposition of \(G\), and each derived bag of size \(b\) requires at least \(db\) vertices in the original bag. This proves the identity.

**Interpretation and scope:** Under Theorem 4.1’s hypotheses, the embedding \(G[K_d]\subseteq H_B\) therefore implies \(\operatorname{tw}(H_B)\ge d(\operatorname{tw}(G)+1)-1\). Substitute all fixed coordinates simultaneously. If the fixed assignment uses only one bit value, generate that constant from an unrestricted input in one gate. ## Observation

For \(F\subseteq\{0,1\}^N\), define the residual after prefix \(p\) by \(R(p)=\{u:pu\in F\}\). At depth \(t\), there are at most \(\min(2^t,2^{|F|})\) distinct residuals, and
\[
R(pb)=\{u:bu\in R(p)\}.
\]

**Proof:** There are \(2^t\) prefixes. Also, each residual is determined by which members of \(F\) extend its prefix, giving at most \(2^{|F|}\) possibilities. The transition identity follows directly from \(pbu\in F\) iff \(bu\in R(p)\).

## Scope and evidence

This is a general fact about finite languages and their exact prefix states. An exhaustive check of all families and prefix depths for lengths through 3 passed 1,082 cases (`cm-79672d3dc61b4afb`); that check is finite verification, not the proof.

## Observation

For a THR∘THR circuit with integer weight matrix \(W\) of positive rational rank \(r\), choose \(r\) independent rows as a basis. A dynamic program can process input variables while counting assignments by their partial sums on those rows. Each state determines every bottom gate’s weighted sum, so at the end it determines the circuit’s output. If \(|W_{ji}|\le M\), there are at most \((2nM+1)^r\) states. The algorithm is exact, with running time polynomial in the input and coefficient bit lengths times this state count.

If \(r=0\), all rows of \(W\) are zero, so every bottom gate and the whole circuit are constant; evaluate the circuit directly.

## Interpretation and scope

This repairs the rank-zero boundary defect in S0267’s claimed runtime. It proves an exact algorithm for low-rank weight matrices, but gives no speed-up for general matrices and no direct P vs NP consequence.

import Mathlib.Data.Nat.Basic
universe u
variable {Solver : Type u}
variable (s : Nat → Nat) (A : Nat)
variable (Plain : (Nat → Nat) → Nat → Solver → Prop)
variable (S tau : Solver → Nat → Nat)
def InfDisj : Prop := ∀ M, Plain s A M → ∀ c d m0 : Nat, ∃ m, m0 ≤ m ∧ (S M m > s m ^ c ∨ tau M m > s m ^ d)
theorem no_tail_bounds (hdisj : InfDisj s A Plain S tau) (M : Solver) (hM : Plain s A M) (c d : Nat) : ¬ ∃ m1 : Nat, ∀ m : Nat, m1 ≤ m → S M m ≤ s m ^ c ∧ tau M m ≤ s m ^ d := by
  intro h
  obtain ⟨m1, hb⟩ := h
  obtain ⟨m, hm, hf⟩ := hdisj M hM c d m1
  have hb' := hb m hm
  rcases hf with hS | ht
  · omega
  · omega

#print axioms no_tail_bounds
evidence.fidelity_reason: `InfDisj` formalizes the infinitely-often disjunction for each `M` satisfying `Plain s A M` and every `c`, `d`, and `m0`. `no_tail_bounds` concludes that no `m1` makes both bounds hold for all `m ≥ m1`. It states no inclusion in a larger transfer class, consistent with the claim’s scope.
evidence.caveat: kernel-checked Lean statement; the fidelity verdict is an independent quality control by a model, NOT a formal proof of equivalence

statement:
statement: For fixed admissible s,A satisfying the stated infinitely-often disjunction, every M in M_{s,A}^{plain} and every fixed c,d has no m1 such that S_M(m)<=s(m)^c and tau_M(m)<=s(m)^d holds for all m>=m1.
derivation: Assume such an m1 exists. Instantiate the infinitely-often disjunction with this M,c,d and m0=m1. It supplies m>=m1 where at least one bound fails, contradicting the assumed simultaneous bounds throughout the tail. The conclusion is confined to the stated solver class and does not establish inclusion in any larger transfer class.

import Mathlib.Data.Bool.Basic
def restrictGate {X Y : Type} (f : (X → Bool) → (Y → Bool) → Bool) (a : X → Bool) : (Y → Bool) → Bool := fun y => f a y
theorem restriction_independent_gates_survive {X Y : Type} (f : (X → Bool) → (Y → Bool) → Bool) (h : (Y → Bool) → Bool) (hi : ∀ x y, f x y = h y) (hn : ∃ y₁ y₂, h y₁ ≠ h y₂) : ∀ a, (∀ y, restrictGate f a y = h y) ∧ ∃ y₁ y₂, restrictGate f a y₁ ≠ restrictGate f a y₂ := by
  intro a
  constructor
  · intro y
    exact hi a y
  · obtain ⟨y₁,y₂,he⟩ := hn
    exact ⟨y₁,y₂, by simpa [restrictGate, hi a y₁, hi a y₂] using he⟩

#print axioms restriction_independent_gates_survive

## Observation

The assigned question is Q-08a1c5b68f. The binding specification requires fixing both state width \(S\) and decoder cost \(D\) when reporting an update-cost minimum. It also distinguishes full search semantics from the weaker live/dead separation variant.

## Established

For full search semantics, at any layer \(t\), if there are \(L_t\) live prefixes and at least one dead prefix, then a correct machine needs at least \(L_t+1\) distinct states: each live prefix must have its own state, and dead prefixes must not share one of those states. With \(S_t\) state bits there are at most \(2^{S_t}\) states, so
\[
S_t \ge \left\lceil \log_2(L_t+1)\right\rceil.
\]
If there are no dead prefixes, the same counting argument gives \(S_t\ge\lceil\log_2 L_t\rceil\). This is a state-counting bound, not an update-gate lower bound.

For Search-MCSP, each circuit computes one truth table, so the full YES set is witness-separated; this recovers \(S\ge\lceil\log_2|Y|\rceil\), including for affine state maps. ## Observation

For a fixed suffix \(z\), let \(W(p,z)\) be the set of valid witnesses for input \(pz\). Suppose a deterministic streaming machine’s final decoder depends only on its final state and is correct whenever \(W(p,z)\neq\varnothing\).

## Lemma

If equal-length prefixes \(p_1,\ldots,p_k\) have nonempty, pairwise disjoint sets \(W(p_i,z)\), then they reach distinct states after reading their prefixes. Hence the machine has at least \(k\) states.

**Proof.** If two prefixes reached the same state, processing the common suffix \(z\) would lead to the same final state and decoded output. That output would have to belong to both prefixes’ disjoint witness sets, a contradiction. ∎

## Scope and continuation

This proves a state-capacity bound for a final-state-only decoder. It does not bound transition gate cost, establish that such a prefix family exists for \(SC_{n,s}\), or imply \(P\ne NP\). **Observation.** The bounded-gate support argument extends to sparse live sets. For a deterministic transducer with \(S\) state bits and at most \(G\) fan-in-two gates per update, after \(t\ge1\) updates the union \(U\) of the input positions affecting the final state has size at most \(S(G+1)^{t-1}\). If \(L\subseteq\{0,1\}^t\) must reach pairwise distinct states, projection onto \(U\) must be injective on \(L\). Hence
\[
|L|\le 2^{S(G+1)^{t-1}}.
\]

Proof: s'=s/(cn). Greedy anti-checker: V_0 = all circuits of size <= s', Y_0 = empty. Step i: for every position y in [N] (a fixed wire x_y) evaluate an approximate count of |{C in V_i: C(y) != x_y}|/|V_i| given (Y_i, x|Y_i, y, x_y) - input length L = O(t n), Stockmeyer approximate counting is in BPP^NP subset Sigma_3 subset P/poly (Karp-Lipton chain) so size L^{a'}; a tournament over the N candidates picks the best (y, x_y): N*L^{a'} gates per step. Elimination: if CC(x) > s then for every nonempty V_i some y kills >= 1/3 of V_i (minimax on V_i: otherwise a distribution over V_i is correct w.p. > 2/3 on every input and the majority of O(n) samples computes x with size O(n s') <= s, contradiction); with approximation >= 1/4. Hence V_t = empty after t = O(s' log s') steps. YES (CC(x) <= s'): the circuit for x is never eliminated. Final test 'V_t empty' is coNP on L bits. Total t*N*L^{a'} = N*s^{K}, K = a'+2, independent of s and beta. With s = N^beta: g_beta(N) <= N^{1+K beta} for all beta in (0,1/2]. c is the constant from the majority step (not necessarily 10).

ST2 INDEPENDENT TRANSFER, STRENGTHENED (author Claude family; owner's sec. 9 argument with P = NP replaced by NP subset P/poly): let S be polylog-uniform AC0_d[2^{m^k}] with r CX rounds, uniformity time m^u. Bit i of X_j is a Sigma_{d'}-TIME[poly(m, L_j, log b)] predicate g_j(i, b, D_<j) with random access to the earlier answers D_<j (padding zeros beyond the description). Assume NP subset P/poly, so PH subset P/poly and Sigma_{d'} has circuits of size n^{c}. Induction: if every earlier answer has size <= m^{K_i}, hardwiring b and D_<j gives a circuit for X_j of size m^{K_j}, K_j = c*O(K_{j-1} + k + u), independent of b. For b > K* = max_j K_j the answer 'a circuit of size m^{K_j} for X_j' is admissible in every round (Teacher only has to exist, no uniformity needed), so X_r has circuit complexity <= m^{K*} < m^b at every large N: S fails for all b > K*. Hence: absolute protocol => NP notsubset P/poly (stronger than Thm 1.7's P != NP). Uses neither Lemma 5.4 nor SearchMCSP.

ST3 SANDWICH - EXACT STRENGTH OF THE TARGET (author Claude family): converse with r = 0: if some fixed L in PH (Sigma_d, time m^u) has a.e. superpolynomial circuit complexity (for every b, CC(L_m) > m^b for all large m), then S(1^N, b) = tt(L_m) is a 0-round absolute protocol (depth d+O(1), size 2^{poly(m)}, uniformity poly(m), b ignored). So: [exists L in PH, a.e. superpolynomial] => [absolute 0-round protocol] => [absolute r-round protocol] => NP notsubset P/poly => P != NP. The Teacher rounds move the target at most between the a.e. and the i.o. form of 'PH notsubset P/poly'. import Mathlib
noncomputable def zeroSet {n : Nat} (x : Fin n → Bool) : Finset (Fin n) := by classical exact Finset.univ.filter (fun i => x i = false)
noncomputable def leftZeros {n : Nat} (k : Nat) (x : Fin n → Bool) : Finset (Fin n) := by classical exact (zeroSet x).filter (fun i => i.val < k)
noncomputable def rightZeros {n : Nat} (k : Nat) (x : Fin n → Bool) : Finset (Fin n) := by classical exact (zeroSet x).filter (fun i => ¬ i.val < k)
theorem at_most_m_zeros_depends_on_counts (n m k : Nat) (x : Fin n → Bool) : (zeroSet x).card ≤ m ↔ (leftZeros k x).card + (rightZeros k x).card ≤ m := by classical unfold leftZeros rightZeros; rw [Finset.card_filter_add_card_filter_not]

#print axioms at_most_m_zeros_depends_on_counts
